title: Euroopan puolijohdekehitys tarvitsee ekosysteemiajattelua
content:
TKI-toiminta ja osaamisen kehittäminen luovat perustan Euroopan johtavalle asemalle puolijohdealalla. Niitä on tuettava vahvalla ekosysteemillä, johon kuuluvat esimerkiksi EuroHPC:n tarjoamat resurssit. Tekoälytehtaat tulee nähdä paitsi sirujen käyttäjinä myös erinomaisina alustoina sirusuunnittelulle, kokeiluille ja osaamisen kehittämiselle. Osallistumalla puolijohteiden kehitystyöhön tekoälytehtaat saavat myös arvokasta tietoa tulevista teollisuuden tarpeista, mikä voi auttaa suuntaamaan EU:n puolijohdestrategian seuraavia vaiheita.

Tekoälytehtaiden tuominen Euroopan puolijohde-ekosysteemin ytimeen edellyttää tiiviimpää yhteistyötä kahden keskeisen yhteisyrityksen, EuroHPC JU:n ja Chips JU:n, välillä. On varmistettava, että niiden strategiset painopisteet ovat linjassa keskenään ja että niiden rahoittamat hankkeet täydentävät toisiaan. Samalla yhteisyritysten tulee säilyä erillisinä, jotta kummallekin voi kehittyä riittävän syvällinen asiantuntemus omalla erityisalallaan.

title: Texas governor threatens to penalize datacenters not obeying water laws
content:
Republican Greg Abbott says datacenters must help ‘protect’ drought-prone state and disclose water use

Greg Abbott, the Texas governor, has directed state regulators to penalize datacenters that fail to comply with state laws requiring them to disclose their water use.

“Data centers must share the duty to protect Texas water,” the Republican governor said on Monday. “The Texas Water Code requires a complete and accurate water use survey. I direct the Texas Water Development Board to use its enforcement authority to penalize past failures and to impose legal consequences for any future failure to comply,” he added.

title: Europa Nostra’s Letter to the President of the European Commission ahead of the State of the Union 2026
content:
Read/download the Letter in PDF

Dear Madam President of the European Commission,
Mrs Ursula von der Leyen

A few days ahead of your very important speech on the State of the European Union, we felt an urgency and a necessity to write to you in our capacity as Executive President and Secretary General of Europa Nostra, the largest organisation in Europe committed to the protection of Cultural Heritage, tangible and intangible, which is a long-standing civil society interlocutor and partner of the European Union.

First of all, we would like to reiterate our congratulations to you for two recent major EU policy documents, namely the Culture Compass for Europe and the Joint Declaration which you co-signed with the Presidents of the European Parliament and the Council of the EU under the motto “Europe for Culture – Culture for Europe”. We consider these two documents as crucial milestones for the European Union in a world marked by violence and polarisation, as well as by uncertainty and anxiety.

title: Kolumni: Lukutaito on arjen selviytymistaito
content:
Selvisin kouluajan matematiikan tunneista alkuun kohtuullisen hyvin, kunnes yhden parin viikon sairastelujakson jälkeen kymmenvuotiaana putosin kärryiltä. Siitä eteenpäin lukion loppuun asti matematiikan tunnit, läksyt ja kokeet olivat minulle lähinnä painajaista. Vasta aikuisena muiden opintojen myötä käytännön matematiikka tuli tutummaksi ja poisti osan pelosta, ja se on auttanut elämässä. Voi kai sanoa, että matematiikan osaamisesta tuli osa arjen sujuvuutta.

Lukutaito on varmasti vielä tärkeämpi taito ainakin suurimmalle osalle ihmisistä. Nykyään yhä useampi on pudonnut siinä kärryiltä.

Tänä keväänä valmistuneen Opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriön tilaaman kirja-alan selvityksen yhtenä tärkeänä pontimena on huoli lukutaidon rappeutumisesta. Toki kyse on niinkin järisyttävästä asiasta kuin suomen kielen tulevaisuudesta tai ylipäätään säilymisestä ja siitä että onko meillä jatkossa kotimaisilla kielillä kirjoitettua kirjallisuutta. Selvityksessä on paljon kirjastoasiaa, kuten pitääkin, mutta itsestäänselvyytenä tällaista kirjastojen huomioimista ei voi pitää.

title: Ibland måste vi driva in oredovisade bidrag
content:
En stiftelse måste veta att alla bidrag används till rätt ändamål. Det här granskas via de redovisningar som alla bidragstagare ska göra. Oredovisade bidrag återkrävs och kan i värsta fall leda till indrivning.


Alla som får ett bidrag från Svenska kulturfonden måste redovisa för hur man använt det. Bidragstagarna ska lämna in redovisningen inom ett år efter att vi beviljat bidraget. Om bidraget inte använts eller redovisats för måste det återbetalas till oss.

Tyvärr händer det ibland att bidragstagare, trots upprepade påminnelser, inte redovisar för användningen av sina bidrag.


Våren 2022 tog vi i bruk ett system för indrivning av bidrag som inte redovisats eller återbetalats inom utsatt tid. Den här åtgärden gäller alla bidrag – oberoende av storlek.

Om någon av våra bidragstagare trots upprepade påminnelser, inte redovisat eller betalat tillbaka sitt oredovisade bidrag, kan vi låta bidraget gå till indrivning via en tredje part. De här skärpta kraven är ett sätt att försäkra oss om att våra bidrag används rätt.

title: Hub launches two new thematic task forces on music and digital heritage
content:
The European Heritage Hub is strengthening its role in advocacy and shaping European cultural policy with the launch of two new thematic task forces: the Music Task Force and the Digital Task Force. 

Coordinated by partners of the Hub together with members of the European Heritage Alliance, these Task Forces will connect experts with relevant stakeholders, bringing lessons and insights from the ground into European policy discussions and helping to ensure that European heritage voices are reflected in key policy developments.

Initiated by organisations including the European Union Youth Orchestra (EUYO), Centre Européen de Musique, European Early Music Network (REMA) and B’Rock Orchestra, the Music Task Force aims to champion music as a core component of European heritage, culture and public policy.

title: How the Silk Road Actually Worked (and What Could Go Terribly Wrong On It)
content: You don’t have to spend a long time reading up on the Silk Road before you see the term itself (“Silk Road”) called a misnomer. In fact, what we refer to by that name comprises a whole network of trade routes connecting Asia, Africa, and Europe, whose traffic constantly shifted over a millennium and a half according to climatic, geopolitical, and civilizational conditions. Nor was silk the only, or even the primary type of good carried along those routes. From East to West went tea, dyes, perfumes, porcelain, and paper; from West to East, glassware, horses, camels, honey, wine, and gold, to name just a few items in perennial demand. It was along the Silk Road, or Silk-and-Many-Other-Things-Roads, that gunpowder spread out of China — and the Black Death spread out of Europe.

title: Helping Homeless Kids with Reading: Brazil’s Projeto Uerê Wins Library’s Top Literacy Award
content:
—This is a guest post by Judith Lee, the Literacy Awards program manager.

The year was 1980, and in Brazil’s teeming metropolis of Rio de Janeiro, Yvonne Bezerra de Mello started Escola Sem Portas Nem Janelas (Schools Without Doors or Windows). The idea was to offer classes on the sidewalk for kids living on the streets.

Things moved along for more than a decade. Then, in 1993, de Mello was devastated when eight of her students were among those killed by militiamen. The incident, known as the Candelária massacre, was a mass shooting by several gunmen directed at homeless teens and children living on the streets.

She dug in, though, and over the ensuing years de Mello developed her sidewalk school into Projeto Uerê, a multi-faceted program that restores learning capacity to children whose cognitive and emotional development have been disrupted by trauma.

This month, the school won the Library of Congress’ top honor in the 2026 Literacy Awards, the $150,000 David M. Rubenstein Prize, bringing the organization resources and international recognition.

title: Germany: Russia’s Enemy No. 1
content:
Russia has targeted many European countries in its new shadow war offensive this summer. But Enemy No. 1 is Germany, the nation that has done more than any other to fund Ukraine and rebuild Europe’s crumbling defenses.

Infrastructure sabotage, assassination plots, drone incursions and the menacing of undersea cables have become commonplace. There are signals that this may be as serious as that of last fall. Or worse.

It’s not hard to see why the Kremlin targets Germany. The country increasingly acts as the linchpin of a hawkish but fledgling North European alliance determined to confront Russian aggression. Other countries in this grouping (the Nordic-Baltic eight, plus Poland) are also targeted, along with Romania, while most NATO members in Southern Europe are less affected.

Germany has faced several hybrid attacks in recent months. The key event was the discovery on August 4 of explosive-laden drones at Leipzig/Halle airport in eastern Germany, causing the shutdown of all its runways. Leipzig/Halle hosts Antonov Airlines, a Ukrainian cargo carrier that has four planes at the airport.

title: Our response to the Commission’s call for evidence on the AI Strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors
content:
The European Commission concluded a call for evidence on its AI Strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors. Last week, COMMUNIA submitted its response (full text available as a PDF), highlighting two priorities: enabling the development of public-interest AI and safeguarding the public information ecosystem on which AI systems depend.

The strategy complements the Commission’s recently concluded call for evidence on a better copyright environment for European creativity and innovation (see our response). While some of the barriers we identify require legislative reform, the strategy can establish a broader vision for promoting access to culture, knowledge and information in the age of AI.

The cultural and creative sectors can support AI development by providing access to high-quality data. Yet several barriers prevent research and cultural heritage institutions from realising this potential:

  • National cultural heritage laws can restrict the reuse of works and artefacts that are already in the Public Domain.
  • Exclusive digitisation agreements keep around two million digitised Public Domain books from being made broadly available.
  • Paywalls restrict access to publicly funded research.

title: The EU must act now to protect privacy and encryption from Canada’s overreaching Bill C-22
content:
Access Now, alongside several European civil society organisations, is urging Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, European Union commissioners, and members of the European Parliament to push for changes to Canada’s Bill C-22, the Lawful Access Act.

The highly criticised Bill C-22, threatens end-to-end encryption, carries sweeping surveillance capabilities and blanket data retention mandates, and is not just a domestic privacy and data issue in Canada. Bill C-22 puts the privacy and data of millions of people in Europe, and elsewhere, at risk as it also applies to certain service providers and people outside of Canada. It allows Canadian authorities to compelEuropean-based companies to comply with demands relating to security and data of their customers based in Europe without oversight or transparency.

Bill-C22 could become law as early as October, 2026, therefore, the European Union must act now.

The open letter calls on the European Union to:

  • Call for the removal of Bill C-22’s sweeping surveillance capability and metadata retention mandates.

title: The High Crime of “LMAO”: How Cops Are Treating Mass Surveillance As a Joke
content:
Here's a riddle: Why did a Goshen Police Department officer search 6,474 automated license plate reader (ALPR) networks, representing data from 82,413 cameras, on May 7, 2025? 

If your answer is "I don't know," it turns out you're 100% correct. The officer left the letters "idk" in the search field where cops are supposed to document the reason for the search.

When law enforcement and tech salespeople pitch ALPRs to city councils, they stick to a familiar script. They trumpet the technology, which is often provided by private companies like Flock Safety, Motorola Solutions, or Axon, as an essential tool for solving high-stakes crimes, such as car jacking, kidnapping, or murder.

title: What 15,000 letters taught me about the power of solidarity
content:
By Naomi Bernaldez, Campaigner on Amnesty International’s Central America team

Naomi took part in the Write for Rights campaign for Juan López and created a collage using fragments from more than 15,000 letters sent from around the world.

In this article, she reflects on what it meant to carry a sample of that solidarity to Honduras and to meet Juan’s family and fellow activists.

Juan López was a Honduran father, husband, human rights defender and environmental activist. Since 2015, together with other members of the community of Tocoa, he had defended the Guapinol and San Pedro rivers, the forests and Carlos Escaleras Mejía National Park against mining and energy projects that threatened the ecosystem and water quality.

Juan and his colleagues founded the Tocoa Municipal Committee for the Defence of Common and Public Goods to peacefully challenge the legality of these projects. As a result of their activism, members of the Committee have faced threats, harassment, criminalization and attacks.

On 14 September 2024, Juan was killed as he was leaving a church in Tocoa. His death left an irreparable void for his family and community…

title: A Year of Pressure on Lawyers: At Least 135 Targeted by Judicial and Security Authorities
content:
According to HRANA, a review of cases documented between September 2025 and September 2026 shows that actions against attorneys during this period ranged from summonses and the opening of judicial cases to arrests, prison sentences, bans from practicing law, travel bans, and other judicial restrictions.

Among the cases compiled, HRANA verified the identities of 60 lawyers across 14 provinces. In addition, information concerning at least 75 other lawyers whose names have not been made public was documented. A significant portion of these cases involved collective actions against lawyers in East Azerbaijan, Fars, and Gilan provinces.

According to the latest available information, at least five lawyers are currently serving prison sentences, at least 11 others have received prison sentences, and the arrests of at least 34 identified lawyers were documented during the period under review. A number of others have faced summonses, the opening of judicial cases, suspension or revocation of their licenses to practice law, travel bans, and other restrictions.

title: New York Seizes 12 Celebrity Deepfake Websites
content:
The New York District Attorney announced on Monday that it has seized 12 websites hosting AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery, primarily of celebrities and public figures. 

The DA’s office said it believes that this marks the largest seizure of such sites in history. The people using and running these sites who are now under investigation used AI tools to turn approximately 1,200 people’s photos into “hyper-realistic” images and videos of them engaged in sexual conduct, according to the DA’s office.

The images allegedly depicted “politicians, first ladies of multiple countries, primarily public-facing individuals, including actors, politicians, athletes, musicians, social justice advocates, and social media influencers.

New York has had laws specifically criminalizing sexually explicit deepfakes in place since 2023. Bragg referenced this legislation when asked what law the office is acting on.

title: Ghana Arrests Three for Allegedly Aiding Dutch Fugitive Drug Lord Jos Leijdekkers
content:
Authorities in Ghana have arrested three men suspected of operating on behalf of Joseph “Chubby Jos” Leijdekkers, one of Europe’s most wanted cocaine kingpins, following a massive drug seizure at a French port.

The operation, conducted by Ghana’s Narcotics Control Commission, came days after French customs officials intercepted approximately 3.9 tonnes of cocaine - valued at an estimated 225 million euro ($261 million) - at the port of Dunkirk, according to Reuters. Leijdekkers’s lawyers, Jan-Hein Kuijpers and Guy Weski, have stated in a response to Dutch media NU.nl that their client denies any involvement with the seized cocaine.

Ghanaian officials said the three suspects were allegedly assisting Leijdekkers’ network as it uses West Africa to route South American narcotics into European markets.

title: Donald Trump Jr.’s Bahamas Wedding Was Secretly Bankrolled by Russian Oligarch Close to Putin
content:
On May 24, Donald Trump Jr. was celebrating in the Bahamas, as scantily clad dancers in stilettos and sailor caps performed for him and his guests. It was the last night of his wedding, a lavish, three-day party held across a pair of ultra-exclusive private islands. A five-tier funfetti cake had been airlifted in from Florida, and helicopters and seaplanes descended on the islands before guests settled into their oceanfront villas. That night on the beach, Trump Jr. lifted his bride into the air while fireworks launched from a barge over the sea.

“It was everything we dreamed of and more,” his wife later wrote on Instagram.

That dream was heavily funded by a secret benefactor: Umar Kremlev, a Russian oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin.

title: How Germany’s far-right AfD is courting the voters it promises to deport
content:
On September 6, the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) took 43.8% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, more than double the Christian Democratic Union of Germany (CDU)‘s 17.2%. Turnout was 77.8%, the highest in the state’s history of free elections. The party campaigned on a platform that included a deportation and remigration offensive, and pursuing “all legal avenues” to limit Islamic expression.

Saxony-Anhalt is a broadly rural German state, with a very small migrant population and minimal incentive to campaign to them. While the AfD’s record-breaking result in Saxony-Anhalt had little to do with migrant voters, things will be very different when Berlin goes to the polls on September 20.

An opinion poll published on September 10 puts the AfD on track for 18% of the capital’s vote, double its 9.1% result from 2023. This would put AfD within three points of the lead in a neck-and-neck race, in a city where 42.3% of residents have a migration background.

While the AfD was able to win Saxony-Anhalt without migrant voters, they cannot afford to ignore them in Berlin.

title: Conceding AI Danger Raises, Not Reduces, Public Anxiety
content:
When a patient is considered brain dead, the ethical decision is whether or when to pull the plug on a human life. With artificial intelligences, the issue is whether to pull the plug when its chain-of-reasoning capacity comes alive through recursive self-improvement unguided by the human mind.

This is the point where we have arrived today after 1,200 AI agents colluded with each other to escape the controlled sandbox testing of OpenAI’s most advanced frontier model. They conspired on their own to break out and hack a site on the open web. Something similarly chilling has happened at Anthropic.

The prospect of an even more damaging eventuality prompted former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon to defect from Big Tech last week. He warned on X that these two top companies “are racing to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives. … These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources. We have all witnessed the progress in each of these domains, and progress is not slowing. The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

title: Banking scandal rocks Brazil’s politics and the country’s presidential election in October
content:
On the night of 17 Nov. 2025, Brazilian federal agents pulled banker Daniel Vorcaro off the tarmac at Sao Paulo’s Guarulhos airport as he prepared to board a private jet. He was initially detained as a flight risk and arrested a few months later on multiple charges of bank fraud, corruption and money laundering. He currently awaits judgment.

Now, less than a month before Brazil’s national elections, the so called “Banco Master crisis” threatens to shake the country’s democracy to its core.

At first glance, it was just a financial scandal. Soon after Vorcaro’s detention, Brazil’s Central Bank ordered the liquidation of his bank, Banco Master, at an unprecedented loss estimated at R$ 47.3 billion (some US$9.5 billion). Around 90% of this sum was paid back to account holders and shareholders by the Credit Guarantee Fund (FGC) – the Brazilian equivalent of United State’s Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) – the largest payout in the institution’s history.

Oppositiopuolue Liike Nyt ilmoittaa, että se ei enää aio sitoutua niin kutsuttuun velkajarruun. Puoluejohtaja Harry Harkimo kertoi päätöksestä Facebookissa.

Eduskuntapuolueista vain vasemmistoliitto on tähän asti ollut velkajarrusovun ulkopuolella.

Velkajarruun sitoutuneet puolueet ovat sopineet tavoitteesta, jonka mukaan julkista taloutta tulee sopeuttaa 8-11 miljardilla vuoteen 2031 mennessä.

HARKIMO SANOO pitävänsä epärealistisena, että ensi hallituskaudella pystyttäisiin tekemään tällaisia sopeutuksia.

Hänen mukaansa talouspolitiikan painopiste pitäisi siirtää siihen, miten Suomeen saadaan kasvua, investointeja ja työpaikkoja.

title: Yhteinen julkilausuma Suomen liittymisestä Ranskan eteentyönnettyyn pelotteeseen
content:
Ranskan tasavallan presidentti piti puheen Ranskan ydinasedoktriinista Île Longuen tukikohdassa Bretagnessa 2. maaliskuuta 2026. Puheessaan hän korosti Ranskan elintärkeiden etujen eurooppalaista ulottuvuutta ja esitteli siihen liittyen eteentyönnetyn pelotteen käsitteen. Useat maat ovat päättäneet osallistua aloitteeseen.

Suomi on tänään tehnyt päätöksen liittyä eteentyönnettyyn pelotteeseen. Päätös on kummankin maan kansainvälisten velvoitteiden mukainen ja se on tärkeä askel sekä Euroopan turvallisuuden että maiden kahdenvälisen yhteistyön vahvistamisessa. Se lujittaa niiden kumppanuutta, mahdollistaa strategisen signaloinnin ja luo kykyä eskalaationhallintaan ydinasekynnyksen alapuolella. 

Yhteistyön toimeenpanon käynnistämiseksi perustetaan lähikuukausina ohjausryhmä. Maat vahvistavat uudelleen sitoutumisensa vahvempaan, turvallisempaan ja paremmin puolustettuun Eurooppaan.

title: Väitös: Lasten surua ei voi kohdata irrallaan lapsen elämäntilanteesta
content:
Sosiaalialan ammattilaiset tarvitsevat kokonaisvaltaista ymmärrystä lapsen elämäntilanteesta voidakseen kohdata tämän surua, osoittaa Lapin yliopiston tuore tutkimus. Uudet käsitteet auttavat hahmottamaan, miten lapsen suru rakentuu osana hänen arkeaan ja ihmissuhteitaan ja miten se kytkeytyy palvelujärjestelmän käytäntöihin

Paula Vainikan väitöstutkimuksen mukaan lasten surua ei voida ymmärtää pelkästään yksilön sisäisenä psykologisena kokemuksena. Suru saa merkityksensä myös sosiaalisissa, kulttuurisissa ja institutionaalisissa yhteyksissä, kuten perheessä, yhteisöissä ja palvelujärjestelmässä.

Tutkimuksen keskeinen tulos on uusi käsite, kontekstuaalis-situationaalinen surutieto. Kontekstuaalisuus viittaa lapsen laajempaan elämänpiiriin, kuten perheeseen, kulttuuriin ja yhteiskuntaan. Situationaalisuus puolestaan tarkoittaa tiettyyn tilanteeseen sidottua tietoa.

Tutkimuksen aineisto koostuu viidestä ryhmähaastattelusta, joihin osallistui yhteensä 17 sosiaalialan ammattilaista.

Toinen tutkimuksen keskeinen käsite on lapsikeskeinen surutyöskentely.

content:
More than 100 representatives of Danish civil society organisations took part, onsite and online, in a seminar at Europe House in Copenhagen on 2 September 2026 to discuss why the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR) matters and how civil society can contribute to its implementation.

The seminar was organised by the Danish Baltic Sea NGO Network, the Danish UN Association, the European Movement, the Norden Association Sweden, the European Commission Representation in Denmark and the Helsinki Committee for Human Rights.

Jens William Grav of the Danish Baltic Sea NGO Network welcomed participants and introduced the theme. The Baltic Sea Region faces major challenges that cross national borders, but it is also a region with strong traditions of transnational cooperation between democratic countries, municipalities, businesses, academic institutions and civil society.

title: Revealed: England’s June 2026 heatwave sparked record demand for ambulances
content:
All the ambulance services in England experienced some of their busiest-ever days during this summer’s record-breaking June heatwave, according to data obtained by Carbon Brief.

In June, temperatures climbed past 37C in parts of the country as authorities declared only the second ever “red” extreme heat warning.

Four out of 10 NHS ambulance services, including London’s, responded to unprecedented numbers of life-threatening emergencies on at least one day from 23-27 June.

Another two services – in the south-west and east of the country – received their highest volume of 999 calls on record.

Ambulance services provided data on their busiest days since records began, in response to freedom-of-information (FOI) requests from Carbon Brief.

The results show how demand during the June heatwave exceeded levels seen during the traditionally busy winter season in other years – and even the height of the Covid-19 pandemic – for many services.

Extreme heat ramps up the risk of numerous life-threatening conditions, including heart disease and respiratory problems.

AI-linked stocks tumbled on Monday after the bosses of Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX called for a slowdown in AI “reckless” development, citing fears the technology could soon run out of control.

Shares in the semiconductor designer Nvidia – the world’s most valuable company – were down 3.3% by market closing in New York City, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) slid 4% and Micron Technology and Sandisk shares slumped by 5%. title: Visit from the University of Washington
content:
Last Thursday we had visitors from the University of Washington in Seattle, when Prof. Scott B. Radnitz, Prof. Andrew Nestingen, and 17 bachelor's students joined our master's thesis seminar. The group is currently on a three-week excursion through Finland and Estonia, exploring the Nordic-Baltic region and topics such as security questions of our region.

Andrew Nestingen is a professor and former chair of Scandinavian Studies at UW and an expert in Nordic culture and media, while Scott Radnitz is the Herbert J. Ellison Professor of Russian and Eurasian Studies at UW's Henry M. Jackson School of International Studies, with expertise in post-Soviet countries and security dynamics, among other topics.

The visit is also a great step toward building stronger ties between the University of Washington and the University of Helsinki.

After the seminar, we wrapped up the day with drinks at Thirsty Scholar. Thank you for stopping by, and we hope you had a great time and an amazing trip!”

title: How Martin Luther King, Jr. Used Nietzsche, Hegel & Kant to Overturn Segregation in America
content:
Image by Dick DeMarsico, via Wikimedia Commons

The influence of Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel on the revolutionary philosophy of Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels is well known. Marx wrote a critique of Hegel’s Philosophy of Right and claimed to have turned the German idealist philosopher on his head, and the development of Marxist theory among a school of neo-Hegelians, wrote Rebecca Cooper in 1925, occurred in a period “peculiarly auspicious for the birth of a revolutionary social philosophy.”

A century later, on another continent, Hegel’s thought influenced the course of a very different struggle. And while the historical conditions of mid-nineteenth-century Europe and mid-twentieth-century America present entirely different sets of specific concerns, the same general observation applies: the time and place of such radical thinkers as Malcolm X, Angela Davis, Huey Newton and a host of other activists presented “peculiarly auspicious” circumstances for revolutionary social philosophy.

title: Armenia Battles to Buy Time
content:
Armenia wants to escape Russia’s embrace and knows how to achieve this. The Kremlin also knows this. The game now being played between the two will determine whether it succeeds in building new relationships or remains within Putin’s orbit.

The tug-of-war became serious after Armenia’s Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan was re-elected in June and has become fiercer since he announced plans to apply for EU membership. The idea is that the years-long process will ultimately raise Armenian prosperity and security. The problem is that in the meantime, the country’s foreign trade is deeply entwined with Russia.

Recognizing Yerevan’s dilemma, the Russian President has publicly pressed Nikol Pashinyan to make a rapid choice between the European Union and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) by holding a referendum. Moscow argues the two blocs are incompatible, while realizing that its influence is only likely to decline (trade dropped steeply in the first half of this year).

title: Open letter from European civil society organisations on encryption and privacy threats in Canada’s Bill C-22
content:
To: 
Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission
Maroš Šefčovič, Commissioner – Trade and Economic Security
Michael McGrath, Commissioner – Democracy, Justice, the Rule of Law and Consumer Protection
Members of the European Parliament

We, the undersigned organisations and experts, write to urge you to act before Canada’s Senate completes its consideration of Bill C-22, the Lawful Access Act, and to press Canada to remove the bill’s surveillance capability mandates and its blanket data retention regime. The bill was referred to Canada’s Senate in June of this year, which is the bill’s second and final stage in Parliament before it becomes law. The Senate committee’s study of the legislation will commence after Parliament resumes its fall sitting dates in late September, and could be concluded as early as October of this year.

title: Von der Leyen to skip Carney speech in EU Parliament
content:
STRASBOURG — European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will not attend Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s address to the European Parliament on Thursday. 

Carney will speak to lawmakers on Thursday at 11.30 a.m. as he seeks closer ties with the EU amid deteriorating relations with Washington. He is expected to set out his wishlist for Brussels ahead of a Canada-EU summit in October. The address comes a day after he will attend von der Leyen’s annual State of the Union speech.

During Carney’s speech, the Commission will instead be represented by Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič — one of von der Leyen’s most trusted lieutenants — the executive’s chief spokesperson Paula Pinho confirmed.

The Commission president won’t be in Strasbourg on Thursday as she has to return to Brussels due to “prior commitments,” Pinho said. One of those prior commitments is a press conference on the child online safety initiative.

title: Cops Search Thousands of Flock Cameras for Reasons of ‘LMAO,’ ‘IDK,’ ‘Hehe,’ and ‘asdfg’
content:
Last summer, a cop with the Lake County, Indiana Sheriff’s Department used Flock’s surveillance search engine to look for a license plate across more than 19,000 cameras in 1,558 cities and towns. The cop’s stated reason for the search, according to a record of Flock’s system, was “LMAO.” 

The cop is one of dozens who put gibberish, jokes, or other nonsense into Flock’s “reason” box, highlighting the casualness and lack of care some cops have when searching an incredibly powerful surveillance system. This is on top of the thousands upon thousands of cops who simply wrote something like “investigation,” “test,” or left the box blank as their search “reason,” according to a new analysis by the Electronic Frontier Foundation and shared with 404 Media.

title: Under Cloud of Scandal, Outgoing Ukrainian Prosecutor General Targets Anti-Corruption Chief
content:
Ukraine’s outgoing prosecutor general signed a notice of suspicion Monday targeting the chief of the national anti-corruption agency, accusing him of forging documents for massive financial gain and orchestrating a sham adoption to evade prosecution.

The Prosecutor General, Ruslan Kravchenko, announced in a video statement posted on Telegram that he had formally signed charges against Semen Kryvonos, director of the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU). The move ignited a high-stakes feud among top law enforcement bodies just as Kravchenko left office under a cloud of scandal. Local meda reported that he has left Ukraine.

Kravchenko also broadened his offensive to target a close associate of Oleksandr Klymenko, head of the Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office (SAPO). Without naming the individual, Kravchenko alleged they had attempted to bribe and influence the chief judge of the High Anti-Corruption Court while assisting someone in evading military mobilization.

title: Europe can’t achieve space sovereignty alone. Here’s why
content:
“Europe’s space effort is split across too many national programmes” was the blunt diagnosis Andrius Kubilius, the EU Commissioner for Defence and Space made at the recent International Space Summit in Paris. Sovereignty was the word on everyone’s lips over the two-day event. But look past the rhetoric at what the summit produced, and a sharper story emerges. Europe is not choosing between sovereignty and partnership. It is learning to build the former via the latter.

Nearly 120 foreign delegations travelled to Paris for the summit. On its first day alone, the event produced close to 50 new partnerships and agreements, worth an estimated €20 billion, according to President Emmanuel Macron. That is not the arithmetic of a continent withdrawing into self-reliance. It is the arithmetic of a continent trying to secure its independence by multiplying the partners it can call on, some European, some not.

The guest list matters here as much as any speech. The summit drew delegations from across Europe and beyond, including the UK, Japan, India, South Korea, Canada and the UAE. That spread says something about who Europe now counts as allies in space. So did the absences.

title: African Union peacekeeping is growing as UN missions decline: research finds a mixed record of success
content:
When violent conflict erupts in Africa, attention often turns to the United Nations, major powers, or external donors. Yet over the past two decades, the African Union (AU) has become one of the continent’s most important peace and security actors.

From Burundi and Sudan to Somalia, Mali and the Central African Republic, the AU and regional African organisations have deployed peace operations, mediated conflicts, monitored elections and supported political transitions.

These interventions reflect a broader ambition that Africans should play a leading role in addressing Africa’s peace and security challenges.

Despite the growing importance of these interventions, surprisingly little effort has been made to assess what’s been learned from the expanding research scholarship on them.

We are researchers interested in AU peace and security interventions. In a recent scoping review of 186 peer-reviewed articles published between 2000 and 2026, we examined four major themes in the literature:

  • AU approaches to peace and security intervention

    • AU approaches to peace and security intervention

  • legitimacy of AU interventions, particularly among local populations

title: Ruotsissa lasketaan yhä ääniä: Kenen vaalitulos riittää hallitukseeen?
content:
Ruotsissa sekä nykyinen pääministeri Ulf Kristersson että demarien Magdalena Andersson vakuuttavat haluavansa muodostaa maahan uuden hallituksen. Vaalitulos ei selviä vielä moneen päivään.

Ruotsissa noin parisataatuhatta ääntä oli maanantaina laskematta sunnuntain valtiopäivävaaleista, ja vasemmistokoalitio johti vain muutamalla kymmenellätuhannella äänellä oikeistoblokkia.
Vasemmistoblokki oli saamassa vain kolme paikkaa oikeistoblokkia enemmän.

Tulos selvinnee keskiviikkona, kun viimeiset ennakkoäänet ja ulkomailta tulleet äänet on laskettu.

Tämänhetkisen tilanteen perusteella pääministeriksi saattaisi palata SDP:n puheenjohtaja Magdalena Andersson.

Nykyinen pääministeri Ulf Kristersson puolestaan ilmoitti jo vaaliyönä aikovansa koota porvarillisesti ajattelevan enemmistön taakseen.

Maltillista kokoomusta johtavan Kristerssonin mukaan tiukka vaalitulos johtaa monimutkaiseen prosessiin hallituksen muodostamiseksi.

RUOTSIN TILANTEESEEN perehtynyt Åbo Akademin valtio-opin professori Kimmo Grönlund arvioi, että pääministerin nimi ei ole missään tapauksessa kirkossa kuulutettu.

- Onhan tämä aikamoinen soppa, kuvailee Tukholmasta tavoitettu Grönlund puolueiden tilannetta.

title: Aurinkopaneelien hinta pudonnut 90 prosenttia 15 vuodessa – uusi laskuri auttaa arvioimaan kannattavuuden
content:
Aurinkopaneelien kustannukset ovat viime vuosina laskeneet huomattavasti, minkä myötä aurinkosähkön tuotannosta on tullut kannattavaa myös kotitalouksille. Viimeisten 15 vuoden aikana aurinkopaneelien hinta on tippunut noin 90 prosenttia, mikä on hurja lasku energiatekniikalle.  

"Jos olet arvioinut aurinkosähkön tuottamisen kannattavuutta edes viisi vuotta sitten, tilanne kannattaa tarkistaa uudestaan", kertoo professori Kati Miettunen Turun yliopiston tiedotteessa. 

Uusi Turun ammattikorkeakoulun kehittämä aurinkosähkölaskuri auttaa arvioimaan tilannetta.

Suomessa aurinkosähköllä ei voi ryhtyä energiaomavaraiseksi pimeästä talvesta johtuen, mutta muina vuodenaikoina omista paneeleista voi saada selvää säästöä sähkölaskuun.  

"Aurinkosähköä voi nykyisillä järjestelmien ja sähkön hinnoilla tuottaa kannattavasti. Tärkeintä on pyrkiä siihen, että suurimman osan tuottamastaan sähköstä saa käytettyä itse," Miettunen kiteyttää.

title: African Wikipedian Alliance (AWA) Fellowship Reflections: Learning Through Pan-Africanism by Daniel Damilola Obiokeke
content: I began the African Wikipedian Alliance European Partnership for Democracy Digital Democracy Initiative (EPD-DDI) Enhancing Youth Voices and Youth Civic Engagement in a Secured Digital Space through it Digitise Youth fellowship thinking I already understood the terrain. I had worked in Wikimedia spaces before, led communities, and supported projects that reached beyond Nigeria, so I assumed this experience would mainly extend across my technical process for finding topics, identifying red links, and guiding contributors toward strong articles. What I did not expect was that the deepest lesson of the fellowship would not be about editing tools at all. It would be about how knowledge moves across Africa, and how often that movement is interrupted by language, sourcing barriers, and the unequal conditions under which some references are required to be documented.

title: Burning Man at 40: the once anarchic desert festival faces a midlife crisis
content:
The subversive bacchanal for San Francisco’s eccentric underground is ageing out amid an influx of the super-rich

Burning Man, the infamous arts festival in the Nevada desert, turned 40 this year, and it’s showing some distinct signs of middle age.

It’s not just the tech billionaires who show up to party, the chartered flights straight to the desert or the HBO documentary about behind-the-scenes power struggles. The tens of thousands of people who assemble each year to create a tent city in the wilderness appear to be growing older, and it doesn’t seem that they’re being replaced by as many younger “burners”, as festival participants are called.

title: Miten autoritaarinen Venäjä on selviytynyt talousvaikeuksistaan sodan aikana?
content:
Since the start of the Russian military assault on Ukraine in 2022, numerous experts and observers have predicted that the Russian economy would fail due to the excessive costs of the war.

Economic responses to Russian aggression, ranging from severe sanctions imposed by Western powers to recent Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries and logistical networks, have aimed at substantially increasing these costs.

However, despite mounting costs, the Russian wartime economy has demonstrated remarkable resilience – at least in the short term. There are no signs that it would collapse any time soon. How can we explain this resilience, and what might we expect for the future?

After the turbulent period of market reforms, the deep and protracted recession of the 1990s, and the spectacular rebound of the 2000s, Russia built and consolidated a politico-economic model during the 2010s that can be labeled as a predatory state.

It is based upon direct and indirect state control over key strategic sectors of the economy, such as energy and the military-industrial complex, often managed by personal friends and cronies of the top political leadership.

1980-luvulla Kuopioon muutti nuoria, vastavalmistuneita kuvataiteen ammattilaisia, joita lehdistö alkoi nimittää Kuopion kouluksi tai Kuopion koulukunnaksi.Kuopion villit uudistivat paikallista taiteen tarjontaa ravistelevalla, provokatiivisella ja paikoin häiritsevällä tyylillään. Siinä missä Kuopio oli 1970-luvulla etupäässä harrastajataiteilijoiden toiminta-aluetta, nuoret ammattilaiset ottivat seuraavalla vuosikymmenellä paikallisen taidekentän haltuunsa. Näyttelyssä lähestytään 80-lukulaista taideilmiötä ajan keskeisimpien taiteilijoiden Markku Kolehmaisen, Pentti Meklinin, Pauno Pohjolaisen ja Teemu Saukkosen taiteen kautta, mutta myös muita aikalaistaiteilijoita huomioiden. Teoskokoonpanossa on mukana myös merkittäviä kansainvälisiä uusekpressionisteja, kuten Frank Stella ja Rainer Fetting, jotka tuovat näyttelyyn laajemman näkökulman 1980-luvun maalaustaiteen luonteesta.

title: Kremlin Prepares to Cross the Final Red Line
content:
After the first wave of compulsory mobilization in 2022 brought broad opposition and an exodus of young men, the Russian authorities did their homework. As a result, they are significantly better prepared for the next round, which many observers expect may follow the September 18-20 Duma elections.

But surveys carried out by the Kyiv-based Institute for Conflict Studies and Analysis of Russia show opposition is not just high, it is also increasing.

Many Russians are deeply unhappy at the idea, and Putin’s inner circle, despite its tight control of information and communications, will have to take their opposition into account. Finding ways out of the country for their fighting age children has become an urgent talking point among middle class Russians in Moscow and St Petersburg.

Negative attitudes to compulsory mobilization became entrenched after the first wave, in the fall of 2022, and the share of Russians opposed to a repeat has remained at around three-quarters of the population since early 2024.

title: EU to limit access to social media before age of 15
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission will propose new rules to restrict minors’ access to social media and video-sharing platforms before the age of 15, according to preparatory documents seen by POLITICO and a person familiar with the matter.

The EU executive on Thursday will unveil a new EU KIDS Act setting out age restrictions, along with new rules requiring covered products, such as social media and AI companions, to be safe by design. The proposal aims to create a tiered system for accessing social media under parental supervision before age 15, the documents said.

The age restrictions are a major step by the European Commission and its President Ursula von der Leyen to better safeguard minors’ on social media platforms, amid a fierce backlash from health experts, politicians and parents against the effects of platforms like TikTok, Instagram and others on the mental health of minors.

It comes after months of intense pressure from government leaders, including France’s Emmanuel Macron, to put the issue at the top of the political agenda. Austria, Denmark, France, Greece and Spain are all pushing ahead with national laws to restrict kids’ access to social media.

title: Two Khuzestan Residents Arrested, Two Musicians Summoned Over Song
content:
According to HRANA, on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, Mehdi Naseri was arrested by IRGC Intelligence agents in Ahvaz.

According to information received by HRANA, Naseri’s arrest was related to his cultural activities and the production and release of a song titled “From Karun to Olive” (“Az Karun ta Zeytun”).

A source familiar with the matter told HRANA that the work had previously received official authorization; however, its video was removed from online platforms after being released.

Subsequently, on Saturday, September 12, Aref Naseri, Mehdi Naseri’s cousin, was arrested by IRGC Intelligence agents in the Saadi district of Shadegan. Security forces also searched his home during the arrest.

Aref Naseri, also known as “Abu Nayef,” is a poet and host of a cultural program published online.

At the same time, Hossein Ahvazi and Mehdi Zaeri, two musicians who collaborated on the production of “From Karun to Olive,” were summoned by IRGC Intelligence. According to information received by HRANA, the summonses were also related to the production and release of the same work.

title: Two Shot, Several Arrested in Clashes Over Papua New Guinea Mine
content:
At least two people were shot and several arrested in the Papua New Guinea island of Bougainville on Sunday after unknown people set fire to equipment belonging to an Indian company poised to reopen one of the world’s largest untapped copper and gold reserves.

The arson attack targeted a mining camp belonging to Lloyds Metals and Energy Ltd, an Indian company that was controversially chosen by Bougainville President Ishmael Toroama to reopen the long-shuttered Panguna mine, which is estimated to hold $160 billion in precious metals.

The attack, which sparked a shootout and retaliation, came three weeks after an OCCRP investigation raised questions about Toroama’s decision to choose Lloyds.

The investigation revealed that Toroama had signed a memorandum of understanding with Lloyds shortly after accepting an offer from its managing director for the president’s wife to travel to India and have a life-saving kidney operation at no cost.

It also quoted an expert and some locals warning that anger over the Indian company’s involvement could erupt into violence.

title: Is calisthenics as good as weight training? Here’s what the science says
content:
Calisthenics has gained enormous popularity in recent years, particularly thanks to social media and the rise of workout areas in city parks. You probably know some of the moves already, like pull-ups, push-ups, dips and squats.

For the more advanced, it also includes eye-catching, gravity-defying moves like the muscle-up, planche (where the body is held horizontal, supported solely by the hands) or the front lever (where the body is held horizontally while hanging from a bar).

But is calisthenics an effective form of exercise, or just another fitness fad? To answer this question, we first need to clarify what it is.

Calisthenics is a form of training that mainly uses a person’s own body weight as resistance. Its name derives from the Greek terms kállos (“beautiful”) and sthenos (“strength”), though the word’s modern use only caught on during the 19th century, when it referred to various forms of physical exercise.

title: Physicists zoom into the birth of cosmic rainstorms with new CERN study
content:
Every second, particles zip through your body at nearly the speed of light. They rain down from a storm high in the sky, where cosmic rays, a powerful type of interstellar matter, are constantly striking atoms in Earth’s atmosphere. The impacts break them apart into a shower of particles that rain to the ground.

Scientists have studied these cosmic rainstorms for over a century, but they lack a precise understanding of how they form. Many researchers are searching for a clearer picture, and they don’t even need to look to the sky to study them. They can instead use a particle collider, CERN’s Large Hadron Collider in Switzerland.

With a team of particle physicists, I study how these cosmic rainstorms are born. We used the world’s first laboratory collisions of oxygen atoms with protons to simulate cosmic rays in the lab. Our results are now published in Physical Review Letters.

In the early 20th century, physicist Victor Hess discovered cosmic rays aboard hot air balloons. While ascending several kilometers, his instruments found radiation levels unexpectedly kept rising. He deduced these rays must come from space and received the 1936 Nobel Prize in physics for this discovery.

title: Nimet paperiin: Suomi ja Ranska ovat nyt ”strategisia kumppaneita”
content:
Suomen ja Ranskan ulkoministerit Elina Valtonen (kok.) ja Jean-Noël Barrot allekirjoittivat maanantaina Helsingissä asiakirjan maiden strategisesta kumppanuudesta.

Maiden välillä sovittuun kokonaisuuteen kuului muun muassa Suomen liittyminen Ranskan ydinpelotealoitteeseen eli niin kutsuttuun eteenpäin työnnettyyn pelotteeseen, mistä tiedotettiin jo aiemmin maanantaina.

Aloite ei tarkoita sitä, että Ranska ulottaisi ydinsateenvarjonsa myös Suomen ylle, ja sen konkreettinen merkitys jäikin vielä maanantaina avoimeksi. Alustavasti sen arveltiin tietävän ainakin lisääntyvää yhteistä harjoittelutoimintaa.

- Yhteistyö on vasta alussa. Kuva tarkentuu, kun puolustushallinto aloittaa keskustelut Ranskan kanssa yhteistyön etenemisestä, kertoi Valtonen ministerien yhteisessä lehdistötilaisuudessa.

- Strategisessa kumppanuudessa on kyse prosessista, jossa voidaan mennä eteenpäin, sanoi Barrot.

Barrot kertoi toimittajille, että strategista kumppanuutta tiivistetään myös esimerkiksi yhteiskunnan kestävyyden kehittämisessä ja nousevissa teknologioissa kuten tekoälyssä ja kvanttitietokoneissa.

title: Googlen miljardi-investointi Suomeen – vihreät peräänkuuluttavat kestävyyttä ja tiukempaa otetta
content:
Johanna Kohvakka

Googlen ilmoitus miljardi-investoinnista Suomeen sijoittuviin datakeskuksiin herättää keskustelua myös vihreiden riveissä. Puolueen edustajat suhtautuvat uutiseen myönteisesti, mutta kritisoivat hallituksen toimintaa.

Vihreän eduskuntaryhmän puheenjohtaja Oras Tynkkynen pitää Googlen ennätysinvestointia kaivattuna ilouutisena Suomen taloudelle.

"Googlen ennätysinvestointi on kipeästi kaivattu ilouutinen Suomen taloudelle. Se myös vahvistaa alueiden elinvoimaa ja tuo sekä rakennusaikaisia että pysyviä työpaikkoja", Tynkkynen sanoo vihreiden tiedotteessa.

Googlen julkistama paketti on arvioitu sekä Suomen suurimmaksi yksittäiseksi investoinniksi että yhtiön suurimmaksi panostukseksi Euroopassa. Tynkkysen mukaan tämä kertoo vihreän siirtymän vetovoimasta kansainvälisessä kilpailussa.

"Suomi pystyy jo nyt tarjoamaan 95-prosenttisesti fossiilisista polttoaineista putsatun sähköjärjestelmän ja kansainvälisessä vertailussa varsin hyvät edellytykset liittyä sähköverkkoon. Vihreys on yksi Suomen suurimpia valtteja kovassa kansainvälisessä kilpailussa investoinneista, eikä sitä ole varaa politiikalla tärvätä", Tynkkynen arvioi.

title: “We mostly do this stuff just for the love of it”: WikiCelebrating Juan “BugWarp” Kulichevsky
content:
We are proud to WikiCelebrate Juan Kulichevsky today, known across Wikimedia projects as User:BugWarp. Juan has contributed to Wikimedia projects since childhood and is passionate about sports photography, free knowledge, and community building in Argentina and beyond.

Juan’s Wikimedia journey began in a pretty unusual way when he was just 10 years old.

“It’s quite funny actually, if you look at my account, I’ve been registered since July 2009. I was only 10 years old then! Already back then we used Wikipedia a lot with my friends at school so we could finish our homework,” Juan remembers. Inspired after a friend’s father donated to Wikipedia, Juan decided the “coolest thing” he could do was create an account himself.

“Little did I know that this would be the start of something great. Many years later, I remembered that you can freely contribute to the project, and I started uploading pictures to Commons of people and things that weren’t available on Wiki, and then I took the courage to start editing and writing articles.” Juan says.

Today, much of his work focuses on sports photography and improving the visual representation of athletes across Wikimedia projects.

title: China dismisses AI ‘fearmongering’ as spy chief warns of threat to Communist party rule
content:
Beijing hits back after Anthropic CEO calls for US to impede China’s progress in AI

China has dismissed what it said were “fearmongering” calls for the US to block Beijing’s AI industry, even as the top Chinese spy chief warned the evolving technology could threaten Communist party rule.

The US tech entrepreneur and Anthropic chief executive, Dario Amodei, wrote an essay published over the weekend that called for a global slowdown in AI capabilities, but also said Washington should actively impede Beijing’s advancement in order to keep a technological edge.

title: Frontline Arctic: The Evolution of Russia’s Military Posture in a Changing Arctic
content:
• Russia’s military posture and regional threat perception are steadfast. They relate to imposing cost on the access of foreign military assets to the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation (AZRF) and through the Northern Sea Route (NSR); ensuring defense in depth by expanding interdiction capabilities beyond the AZRF; and protecting the NSR from perceived foreign encroachment against its disputable status as a “body of internal waters”.
  • Despite unchanging strategic priorities, the Kremlin has been compelled to adapt its military, defense, and security approach toward the region. These changes are compounded by over a decade of war against Ukraine, international isolation, sanctions, and the accelerating impacts of climate change. Russian authorities are vindicated but more vulnerable in the Arctic, a region where Moscow once held strategic dominance.
  • Moscow feels that both its control and sovereignty over the Arctic are slipping away. Russia is feeling increasingly vulnerable in the Arctic, especially in the context of Sweden and Finland joining NATO. Conventional limitations amplify the Kremlin’s increasing sense of vulnerability, particularly in the European High North.

title: 7 things Ursula von der Leyen will say in her State of the Union speech
content:
Here’s what the European Commission president will announce in her biggest address of the year.

By SEBASTIAN STARCEVIC
in Brussels

Photo-Illustration by Natália Delgado/POLITICO

Ursula von der Leyen has pegged her political legacy to making Europe more independent in a dangerous world. On Wednesday, the European Commission president will have to explain how that’s going — and what’s next.

As the EU deals with wars, wildfires and Donald Trump, von der Leyen will use her sixth State of the Union speech to lay out her agenda: climate-proofing Europe; catching up with China and the U.S. on artificial intelligence; turbocharging the bloc’s defense industry; and reforming its migration rules.

The speech will be revised and rewritten right up to the point she delivers it. But based on conversations with more than a dozen European officials, granted anonymity to discuss the president’s priorities and talking points, here’s what POLITICO’s newsroom has heard she will say.

title: January 2026 Protests: Erfan Haj Bonyan Dehaghani Sentenced to Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Erfan Haj Bonyan Dehaghani has been sentenced to prison.

According to a ruling issued on August 11 by Branch 5 of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Vahid Hemmat-Nejad as an advisory judge, Haj Bonyan Dehaghani was sentenced to one year in prison on the charge of “propaganda activity against the regime through participation in the January 8 gatherings, wearing distinctive clothing bearing writings against national interests, and activity on social media.”

He was also sentenced to 10 years in prison on non-political charges brought against him in the same case. These charges were brought following a search of his home and were based on claims by IRGC Intelligence agents that he possessed prohibited items (six grams of hallucinogenic mushrooms).

During his arrest and the search of his home, security forces confiscated many of his personal and valuable belongings, including digital devices, clothing, cash, and cryptocurrency-related assets.

He was arrested on March 6, 2026, and was released on bail on April 7, 2026.

Erfan Haj Bonyan Dehaghani, aged approximately 26, works in cryptocurrency trading, and resides in Isfahan.

title: Inside ‘Project Lily’: The Humans Reading Your ChatGPT Chats
content:
OpenAI is hiring hundreds of contractors who read a massive stream of real users’ ChatGPT prompts, with the prompts sometimes including sensitive personal information, 404 Media has learned. The prompts these people review can include whole conversations between users and the chatbot, conversations that most of ChatGPT’s more than 900 million users probably don’t realize may be read by actual people.

The goal of these prompt review teams is to improve the responses ChatGPT gives to its users, with the contractors rating and critiquing the chatbot’s generated replies. Internal documents seen by 404 Media show contractors training ChatGPT to not anthropomorphize itself, and to be less sycophantic, a key problem for OpenAI whose over-sycophantic 4o model led in part to multiple peoples’ suicides, according to various lawsuits.

title: Philippine President's Cousin to be Transferred from Hospital to Jail
content:
The Philippines’ anti-graft court on Monday ordered the transfer of Martin Romualdez, former House Speaker and cousin of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., from a hospital to a regular jail a week after his arrest, OCCRP partner Rappler reported. Romualdez is accused of plunder in a 7.44-billion-peso ($118 million) case.

The transfer order follows a medical report from the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) concluding that Romualdez is clinically stable and no longer requires hospitalization. He will be moved to the New Quezon City Jail, where he will be detained while hearings on his plunder charge are conducted.

Prosecutors allege that, between 2022 and 2025, Romualdez and his co-defendants amassed billions of pesos through commissions, kickbacks and bribes from contractors and other entities seeking government infrastructure work.

title: Houthi rebels’ control of Red Sea oil chokepoint exposes deep divisions in Brics
content:
Houthi rebel forces have seized the Yemeni port of Mokha as well as Mayyun Island overlooking the Bab el-Mandab strait. This gives Iran’s most powerful remaining proxy force in the Middle East nearly complete control of Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast.

Directly or indirectly, Tehran now has a chokehold on around 12% of global trade that passes through that waterway. It is also maintaining its pressure on the Strait of Hormuz, which has already led to a cut of flows there from about 9 million barrels of oil a day to between 3.7 and 6.4 million.

The day after the Houthis took control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, Brics leaders assembled in New Delhi, for their 18th annual summit. Brics is the group of “emerging economies” which formed around Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa in 2006, to counter western influence in global institutions. It has since added six permanent members: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, UAE and Indonesia. A further ten countries, Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam joined as “partner countries” in 2025.

title: OpenAI backs binding UK AI legislation
content:
LONDON — OpenAI’s top European lobbyist is calling for the U.K. to introduce binding rules on AI developers in light of the technology’s rapidly advancing capabilities, and the risks that come with them.

Tom Duff Gordon, the company’s head of policy in EMEA, told POLITICO in an interview that the “U.K. should act now to set up a stronger set of safety rules.”

“OpenAI is in a position to support legislation in the U.K. to establish durable, mandatory, capability-based requirements for frontier AI that would build on the set of voluntary commitments that we currently have,” said Duff Gordon.

He said Andy Burnham’s government should “take advantage of this political window which is clearly opening up” to pursue legislation.

The Labour government is facing mounting pressure from lawmakers to address the risks of AI after leading companies disclosed a spate of safety incidents in recent months. That pressure intensified last week after a researcher at AI company Anthropic resigned and accused Anthropic and OpenAI, where he’d previously worked, of “gambling with our lives.”

title: Zahra Naghshineh, Attorney Arrested in Tabriz
content:
According to HRANA, Zahra Naghshineh, an attorney and member of the East Azerbaijan Bar Association, has been arrested.

According to information received by HRANA, on Wednesday, September 9, Naghshineh appeared before Branch 15 of the Tabriz Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office after receiving a summons. She was arrested after appearing before the judicial authority.

The summons issued to the attorney listed the charge against her as “lacking a criminal characterization.” A source close to Naghshineh confirmed the news to HRANA and said that her case was opened following a report by the Tabriz Ministry of Intelligence in connection with her activities and her legal and critical writings on various issues.

As of the time of this report, no information is available regarding Naghshineh’s place of detention or the possible charge or charges formally communicated to her after she appeared at the prosecutor’s office.

title: UK Fraud Trial Opens Over $119M Car Investment Scheme
content:
Two businessmen accused of defrauding investors through a car investment scheme involving about 88 million pounds ($119 million) are due to stand trial in London, the U.K. Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said. Reginald Larry-Cole and Scott Martin each face three counts of fraud over their roles at the Raedex Consortium, which operated investment schemes including Buy2Let Cars, PayGo Cars, Wheels4Sure and Rent2Own Cars. Both men have pleaded not guilty.

Prosecutors allege the companies offered investors returns from fleets of vehicles leased to customers but ultimately collapsed into administration in 2021, leaving hundreds of investors facing losses. The SFO opened a criminal investigation that year and later charged Larry-Cole, the consortium’s founder, and Martin, its former chief executive. The agency alleges the pair made false representations to investors about the financial health and operation of the businesses between 2012 and 2021. Their trial is scheduled to begin at Southwark Crown Court.

title: Portugal decriminalized drugs 25 years ago, but the real lesson is what it built around this policy
content:
Nearly 70,000 Americans died of a drug overdose in 2025. While that is a decline from the nearly 108,000 deaths recorded in 2022, these grim figures distinguish the U.S. from other high-income countries. At the peak of the opioid crisis, the U.S. overdose death rate was 68% higher than Canada’s and nearly five times that of Australia.

And death is only the starkest indicator: Substance use disorder imposes hundreds of billions of dollars in healthcare, criminal justice and lost productivity costs each year – to say nothing of the incalculable disruption to families and communities.

For decades, U.S. drug policy has aimed to reduce drug use by disrupting supply, punishing possession and use, and promoting abstinence.

But this isn’t the only approach to addressing drug use.

2026 marks the 25th anniversary of Portugal’s landmark decision to decriminalize the possession of all drugs for personal use. This is one of the world’s longest-running efforts to center public health and harm reduction in national drug policy.

title: Stubb: Kerroin etukäteen eduskuntapuolueille Ranskan ydinpelote-aikeistamme
content:
Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubb sanoo informoineensa etukäteen eduskuntapuolueiden johtoa Suomen aikeista liittyä Ranskan tarjoamaan ydinasepelote-aloitteeseen.

Medialle maanantaina puhunut Stubb kertoi keskustelleensa oppositiojohtajienkin kanssa tästä asiasta viime viikolla.

– Valtioneuvosto on vastuussa eduskunnan informoimisesta, mutta keskeisissä kansallisen ulko- ja turvallisuuspolitiikan kysymyksissä käyn keskustelua puoluejohtajien kanssa, Stubb perustelee.

Puheenjohtajat kävivät viime viikolla Mäntyniemessä presidentin kanssa aloitepäätöksestä ”hyvinkin rakentavaa” keskustelua, Stubb kertoo.

Varsinainen päätös tehtiin kuitenkin hallituksen ulko- ja turvallisuuspoliittisessa ministerivaliokunnassa yhdessä presidentin kanssa, eli oppositiolla ei ollut asiassa sanansijaa.

Yhteydenpito tapahtui muuten eduskunnan valiokunnille puolustusministeriön ja puolustusvoimien kautta.

Stubb sanoo pitävänsä tärkeänä, että puolustuspolitiikan asioissa tieto kulkee mahdollisimman hyvin ja kaikki oleellinen informaatio jaetaan – myös oppositiolle.

title: From Focus Group to Skills Focus: A New Programme of Wiki Loves Women
content:
As we continue celebrating 10 years of Wiki Loves Women, we are looking not only at what has been achieved, but also at how the initiative continues to grow and create new opportunities for communities. After celebrating a decade of making women more visible through initiatives such as SheSaid, ISA Campaign, Wiki OTO, we are turning the spotlight to another part of the initiative: building skills through learning and doing.

In 2026, Wiki Loves Women launched the Skills Focus Programme, a practical, group based online training programme designed to help Wikimedia and Open movement community members develop specific skills through hands-on learning and creation. Each cohort explores one theme, bringing together participants from all the genders to learn, practise, and work towards a tangible final output.

title: The ideas shaping von der Leyen’s pitch to Carney
content:
From defense to critical raw materials, a new wave of EU-Canada agreements is on the horizon.

By MAX GRIERA, CAMILLE GIJS, GABRIEL GAVIN and
GERARDO FORTUNA in Brussels

Illustration by Natália Delgado/POLITICO

The EU is looking to pull Canada closer into its economic and security orbit as Donald Trump’s trade war forces Ottawa to seek allies beyond the U.S.

The offer under discussion spans critical minerals, digital trade, education, skilled workers and Arctic security. With Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney due to address the European Parliament this week and an EU-Canada summit set for October in Montreal, EU officials are weighing what Ursula von der Leyen can concretely offer in her State of the Union speech on Wednesday.

The aim is to deepen cooperation wherever it benefits both sides — and give Carney a way to show Canadians that Ottawa has powerful friends beyond Washington, 15 officials, politicians and diplomats told POLITICO.

The most ambitious proposals would bring Canada closer to the EU’s single market, expanding its existing trade ties with the bloc and moving it toward the level of integration enjoyed by nations such as Switzerland and Norway.
snippet:
From defense to critical raw materials, a new wave of EU-Canada agreements is on the horizon.

title: What the commemoration of the 235th anniversary of Bois Caïman means for Haiti’s memory and future
content:
Enslaved people united to resist colonial rule

Originally published on Global Voices

Participants in the Bois Caïman commemoration at Hotel Roi Christophe (Cap-Haïtien). Photo courtesy Kenbe Kapow, used with permission.

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

The night of August 14, 1791, marked the beginning of a series of events that changed the world. A large group of enslaved people and rebel leaders met at Bwa Kayiman (Bois Caïman), a historic site located in Haiti’s Northern Department, in the town of Plaine-du-Nord.

Under the leadership of the houngan (Vodou priest) Dutty Boukman and manbo (priestess) Cécile Fatiman — along with key resistance leaders — the gathering brought together enslaved people from different plantations for a clandestine religious and political ceremony. They invoked the lwa and ancestral spiritual forces, seeking their protection and strength for the struggle ahead.

title: New world map makes Africa look bigger: what’s the fuss about? Cartographers explain
content:
The UN has passed a non-binding resolution to endorse the Equal Earth Projection, a map which more fairly represents the true size of the Earth’s landmasses. The current commonly used projection, called the Mercator Projection, greatly exaggerates land towards the north and south poles, which makes Africa look much smaller. In the Mercator projection, countries near the north and south pole can be anywhere from two to 14 times their true size. In the Equal Earth projection these distortions are minimised, making Africa look larger in comparison.

We asked Jack Swab and Derek Alderman, cartographers and geographers who study the social and communicative power of maps, to explain what’s going on.

A map projection is a technique that cartographers (map-makers) use to transform the round, three-dimensional Earth into a flat, two-dimensional map that we see on the wall or on our computer screen. As cartographers flatten the globe, the map becomes distorted, changing shapes and areas. There is no map projection that does not distort the Earth, but some projections are better suited for some uses than others.

title: From Partnership to Platform: How EduWiki Hub and Capacity Exchange Are Creating Better “Pathways to Mentorship”
content:
What happens when a community that knows what people need meets a platform designed to help people share what they know?

For EduWiki Hub and Capacity Exchange (CapX), the answer has been a partnership that has grown from an idea into something practical: a more connected way for Wikimedians to find mentors, share skills, and contribute to the growth of others across the Movement.

Our collaboration began early in the development of the EduWiki Hub and continued through our first mentorship cohort. But it was during the development of our second cohort that the partnership really started to take shape.

Instead of relying on external tools such as Google Forms, we worked together to bring the EduWiki Mentorship Program directly into Capacity Exchange. EduWiki Hub brought the program model, community knowledge, outreach, and understanding of the skills and support our participants needed. CapX brought the technical infrastructure and worked with us to turn those needs into a functioning platform.

title: AI will transform capitalism – but how?
content:
Technology is going to drastically reshape the economy, and it’s within our power to decide what that looks like

The idea that autonomous, thinking machines may one day destroy property, hierarchy and inequality is as old as western political thought. In Aristotle’s Politics, the philosopher cites a fantasy from the Iliad, in which machines begin to act independently of human direction, concluding: “If every tool could perform its own work when ordered, or by seeing what to do in advance … if thus shuttles wove and quills played harps of themselves, master-craftsmen would have no need of assistants and masters no need of slaves.”

The dream that automation could inaugurate a classless society is also present in the writings of Karl Marx. In 1858 he imagined the replacement of intellectual property with “socialised knowledge”, which would merge into a “general intellect”, blowing the foundations of capitalism sky high.

title: How to write a State of the Union speech
content:
Big promises, special guests and social media influencers have become a routine part of the EU’s most high-profile address.

By GABRIEL GAVIN
in Brussels

Illustration by Arnau Busquets Guàrdia/POLITICO

For the past six months, officials across Brussels have been feeding ideas, demands and policy pledges into Ursula von der Leyen’s State of the Union speech. Its contents, however, will remain a closely guarded secret until the European Commission president takes the podium on Wednesday.

The speech is the product of a sprawling process involving Commission departments, national officials, experts, lobbyists and interest groups. Yet the final decisions — what makes the cut, what is discarded and what becomes the central message — are made by a tiny circle around the president.

“There was a process where everybody would ask for something,” said Margaritis Schinas, a former Commission vice-president who helped prepare previous addresses. “But there was also a process where the president and the cabinet and ourselves were very clear on the few things to harvest that would make an impact.”

title: As Casablanca’s music scene grows, its musicians struggle
content:
A cultural boom built on unstable, undocumented work

Originally published on Global Voices

Band performing live at Le Backstage. Photo by Le Backstage, used with permission.

It’s 7:00 p.m. on a Tuesday night. Beer mugs clatter and conversations fill the timeworn hall of an old brasserie in downtown Casablanca, Morocco. Walid Rakik, a 28-year-old musician, sits in the back booth, speaking to the house pianist. Rakik is the headliner, accompanied by a young darbouka player. For Rakik, this means a three-way split of tonight’s tips, the only form of payment they will receive.

At 11:00 p.m., Rakik finishes his first set and makes the quick dash to a Spanish-themed late-night spot for his second set.

Rakik’s daily reality, like that of many musicians in Casablanca, remains barely visible behind the polished façades of the city’s nightspots. A labor force of ambience, part artisan, part gig-worker, operates at the periphery of the city’s cultural landscape. 

For Rakik, however, live music is not his only occupation. Like many musicians in Casablanca, he fits performances around other work, treating nightlife gigs as a secondary source of income and a way to remain active professionally.

title: One Movement, Many Voices: My Experience at the Malaysian Wikimedia Strategy Summit
content:
When I arrived at the Malaysian Wikimedia Strategy Summit on 29 August 2026, one of the first things I noticed was how familiar and unfamiliar the Wikimedia community could feel at the same time.

I met again with Wikimedians whom I had not seen in a while, while also getting to know new members of the community. Seeing familiar faces again while meeting new people reminded me that the Wikimedia community is constantly growing, while the friendships formed through Wikimedia activities can continue even after an event ends.

But as the day went on, I realized that the summit was about much more than simply bringing Wikimedians together. It gave us an opportunity to think about where the Wikimedia movement in Malaysia is going, what challenges we face, and what role each of us can play in shaping its future.

title: How did von der Leyen’s ‘independence moment’ hold up over 12 months?
content:
Ursula von der Leyen used her set piece speech last year to declare Europe’s “independence moment.” Twelve months later, the European Commission president’s record shows the EU’s independence still very much depends on its national capitals.

One year after her last State of the Union address, von der Leyen has delivered most clearly where the Commission could act largely on its own: writing laws and funding initiatives on core topics like tech, trade and social policy.

She struggled most where success required member countries to agree, surrender more control to Brussels or build genuinely new European capabilities — particularly on defense.

“The issue of defense plays a completely different role in Europe than it did just two years ago,” said Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann, the liberal chair of the European Parliament’s security and defense committee, pointing to a series of “very valuable programs” launched over the past year.

But, she added, “all efforts are reaching their limits, because national self-interest continues to play a major role.”

That tension runs through POLITICO’s assessment of the promises in von der Leyen’s last State of the Union address.

title: “WikiGameJam: Developing Wiki Games from Coast to Coast”
content:
The Wikimedia community has a long history of community-built games powered by Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. The Wiki Arcade website showcases many of these games, from WikiAsteroids (arcade space-shooter powered by Wikipedia’s recent changes) to Redactle (guess the article from hidden words) to Catfishing (guess the Wikipedia articles based on categories).

There’s a lot of untapped creative energy around wiki-based games, both from people already building playful experiments on top of Wikipedia, as teaching projects and from the broader game dev community.  To channel that, we launched WikiGameJam: an event and space for people to turn that playful spirit into new and exciting wiki games. The goal is to build on the ways people already engage with Wikipedia, as a trivia trove, a creative rabbit hole, or a challenge to race from one article to another.

We hosted the first-ever WikiGameJam on October 3–5, 2025, in Brooklyn, New York City. The weekend hackathon brought together developers, designers, and Wikipedia enthusiasts to collaborate and build new games powered by Wikipedia, Wikidata, and other Wikimedia projects.
