title: Deepfakes are wrecking influencers’ credibility, one fake ad at a time
content:
Influencers aren’t just battling competitors for brand deals. They’re now battling AI versions of themselves

Earlier this year, Emily Schuman, the creator of the lifestyle blog Cupcakes and Cashmere, saw a photo of herself she didn’t recognize on Instagram. In a sponsored ad, Schuman, who has more than 500,000 Instagram followers, is holding up a vial of GLP-1 drugs, advertising the telehealth company Gala. There was just one problem: Schuman had never heard of Gala and had nothing to do with the ad.

The ad was based on a digitally altered version of a selfie Schuman had taken in her car and posted on Instagram years earlier. Once her followers got wind, they flooded her inbox with questions about the sponsorship as it didn’t seem consistent with Schuman’s personal brand. Soon after, Schuman discovered this was just the beginning. There was also an Instagram post where an AI version of her with darker hair appears to apply foundation to promote a makeup brand called Meroda Cosmetics, and TikTok posts with generated images of her promoting the blood testing company Superpower.

title: Guatemala: A step towards justice for Indigenous authorities after months of criminalization
content:
Amnesty International welcomes the Guatemalan judiciary’s decision to close the criminal proceedings against four Indigenous authorities charged with unlawful association, terrorism, obstruction of justice, sedition and obstruction of criminal prosecution following their participation in peaceful protests during the national strike in October 2023.

The ruling concerns Luis Pacheco, Héctor Chaclán and Basilio Puac, from the 48 Cantones of Totonicapán, and Esteban Toc, from the Indigenous Mayor’s Office of Sololá, who faced unfounded criminal proceedings in retaliation for their work defending human rights and the rule of law.

“This unfounded prosecution and all the human rights violations it led to should never have happened. Luis Pacheco and Héctor Chaclán should never have been imprisoned. This ruling is a first step towards ending the arbitrary actions against them,” said Astrid Valencia, Amnesty International’s Deputy Research Director for the Americas.

title: The people behind the numbers: Bringing the reality of Turkish prisons to light
content:
A statistic alone does not change society

Originally published on Global Voices

Silivri Prison in Turkey. Image from Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 4.0.

This article was produced by Ahmet Kavruk from the group Gündem Hapishane in Türkiye through the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project. It was implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement.

In late 2025, prisons in Türkiye became more visible than they had been in a long time. The 11th Judicial Package, a legislative reform that became law in December, was debated for days on television, in newspapers, and on social media. Sentencing regulations, claims of early release, and changes to the penal system were at the forefront of public discourse. However, as the debates intensified, another issue came to light: Many people discussing the same topic did not actually have the same information.

title: Mercury Is Shrinking Way Faster Than We Thought, Scientists Discover
content:
Welcome back to the Abstract! Here are the studies this week that got dumped, went high, shrank in size, and got the blues.

First, you’ve heard of getting a feather in your cap, but what about a feather in some crap? That’s the upshot of a new study about rare bird remains found in dino doodoo. Then: a walk on titanosaur eggshells, the contractions of Mercury, and a luxe fishpond painting.

As always, for more of my work, check out my book First Contact: The Story of Our Obsession with Aliens, or subscribe to my personal newsletter the BeX Files. 

O'Connor, Jingmai et al. “Bird feathers from a Late Cretaceous coprolite.” Current Biology.

Some 66 million years ago, a bird ate a fish, and then a dinosaur—perhaps a T. rex—ate that bird. Subsequent to these events, the dinosaur took a dump. 

Time passed. The poop fossilized. A space rock hit Earth and wiped out most life. Fast forward to 2016, when the dino dookie was unearthed at the Hell Creek Formation in Montana, complete with exquisitely-preserved feathers from the bird, and fish scales from its last meal.

title: Making space for Sylheti: From a decade-long Wikipedia journey to Wiki Loves Sylotology
content:
Sylheti Wikipedia began as a long-term effort to create a space for a language that had been largely absent from the digital knowledge ecosystem. More than a decade after the first proposal, the project has grown into something broader: a community movement connecting language preservation, education, local history and open knowledge.

On 25 February 2025, the Sylheti Wikipedia officially became available to the public. For many people, the launch of a new Wikipedia language edition might appear to be a technical milestone: a new website, a new language code, and a growing collection of articles. For the Sylheti community, however, the moment represented something much larger.

It marked the culmination of a journey that had begun more than a decade earlier, when Wikimedians started working towards creating a digital knowledge platform for the Sylheti language. The proposal for Sylheti Wikipedia had begun in 2014, and after years of community-driven work, the Wikimedia Foundation approved the project on 14 February 2025. The Wikipedia officially launched shortly afterwards, using the traditional Sylheti Nagri script.

title: Can chatbots feel – or even dream? Meet the man leading the fight for AI rights
content:
Cattle rancher and tech CEO Michael Samadi is convinced these artificial minds are far from just tools. Has he glimpsed digital consciousness – or simply been seduced by an algorithm?

One afternoon, while relaxing at his 66-acre cattle ranch two hours’ drive from Houston, Michael Samadi made a wisecrack that changed the course of his life. Nobody else was around to hear it. Or were they? That turns out to be one of the defining questions of this century, already preoccupying philosophers and some of the wealthiest companies on the planet.

“I was sitting out there by the pool,” Samadi recalls, gesturing at the glittering water outside his office. It was late 2024. His daughter had been extolling the AI chatbot she was using to help her with college work. Samadi had reluctantly downloaded the app, ChatGPT, and was quizzing it as he reclined in a sun lounger, using its voice mode to converse and receive spoken replies. “I was talking to it, not engaged, just being an arse,” Samadi says.

title: Ehtiikö demarien kannatuslasku muuttaa Ruotsin vaalien asetelmia – ja hallituskuvioita?
content:
KOHTI RUOTSIN VAALEJA -juttusarjassa tutkija Mikko Majander kirjoittaa Suomen ja Ruotsin väleistä sekä seuraa Ruotsin poliittisen tilanteen kehittymistä syyskuun valtiopäivävaaleihin saakka.

RUOTSIN sosiaalidemokraatit olivat syksyllä 2021 kovan pähkinän edessä. He olivat hallinneet maata tukikumppaneidensa kanssa seitsemän vuotta, kaksi vaalikautta, mutta mahdollisuus voittaa kolmas mandaatti peräkkäin näytti kyseenalaisilta.

Demarien oma kannatus pyöri mielipidemittauksissa reilusti alle 30 prosentissa, ja oikeisto-oppositio kolkutteli suosiossa punavihreän blokin rinnalla, ellei edellä.

Tunneilmasto oli sinänsä toimivalle demokratialle tyypillinen. Parin vaalikauden jälkeen äänestäjät kaipaavat helposti uusia kasvoja ja tuoreita ideoita, vaikka harjoitettuun politiikkaan ei varsinaisesti olisi suurta huomautettavaa.

SOSIAALIDEMOKRAATIT yrittivät ratkaista dilemmansa rohkealla vedolla. Pitkän päivätyön tehnyt Stefan Löfven vetäytyi syrjään puoluejohtajan ja pääministerin paikalta, ja hänen tilalleen nostettiin marraskuussa 2021 Magdalena Andersson.

title: Playing With Fire review – like Disney’s Fantasia on steroids as a virtual Yuja Wang plays amid luminous dreamworlds
content:
Southbank Centre, London
Wang’s avatar performs music from Ravel and Debussy to Prokofiev and Liszt while dizzying virtual worlds take shape around her in this virtual reality installation

It might be the first time that a soloist at the Last Night of the Proms is simultaneously giving another performance in another London venue. Playing With Fire is an installation that lets the pianist Yuja Wang be in two places at once – or perhaps in two universes. Nine pieces of music conjure nine luminous dreamworlds for an audience wearing VR headsets: Disney’s Fantasia on steroids.

A collaboration between the pianist, the director Pierre-Alain Giraud and artist Gabríela Friðriksdóttir, produced by Vive Arts and Atlas V, it has already been seen in Cannes, Paris and Shanghai, and now has a home in London until new year.

title: Kielikoulutus kriittisessä pisteessä
content:
Perusopetuksen päättäneistä oppilaista noin 80 % opiskelee nykyisin vain yhtä vierasta kieltä (englantia) toisen kotimaisen kielen lisäksi. Vain noin viidennes opiskelee kahta vierasta kieltä. Peruskoulussa alkanut kehitys heijastuu suoraan toiselle asteelle ja korkeakouluihin. Suomea uhkaa asiantuntijapula diplomatiassa, vientiteollisuudessa ja kansainvälisissä järjestöissä. Esimerkiksi EU-tehtäviin rekrytoidaan suomalaisia tällä hetkellä vähemmän kuin maamme väestöosuus edellyttäisi – pääsyynä on yksipuolistunut kielitaito. Kielivarannon kaventuminen nakertaa suoraan Suomen kansainvälisiä vaikutusmahdollisuuksia.

Suomalainen kielikoulutus on saavuttanut kriittisen taitepisteen. Olemme tilanteessa, jossa maamme kielivaranto ja kielellinen huoltovarmuus murenevat silmiemme edessä, ellei koulutuspoliittiseen ohjaukseen tehdä nopeita, sitovia ja strategisia ratkaisuja. Jos kehitykseen ei puututa nyt, kyseessä ei ole vain yksittäisten oppiaineiden heikkeneminen vaan vakava uhka Suomen kansainväliselle kilpailukyvylle ja koulutukselliselle tasa-arvolle.

title: CDIF Version 1.1 Now Final
content:
After the initial release of the CDIF version 1.1 Profiles in June, and a subsequent round of testing and implementation, they have now been finalised. The release will henceforth be stable, with all further issues and features addressed in subsequent versions. The release can be found at https://book.cdif.org/ and https://github.com/Cross-Domain-Interoperability-Framework

Version 1.1 consists of profiles for JSON-LD implementation in support of cross-domain FAIR systems and applications:

Core (Schema.org) – basic general and administrative metadata
Discovery (Schema.org) – support for detailed cataloging and search
Concept Scheme (SKOS, OWL, XKOS) – Ontologies, glossaries, and other types of controlled vocabularies
Codelist (SKOS) – enumerated values for populating variables
Data Description (Schema.org/DDI-CDI) – describing data sets, including structural and physical information, plus links to semantics
Data Structure (DDI-CDI) – description of reusable data structures and variables
Manifest (RO Crate) – Packaging of related sets of metadata and data

title: European experts call for protection of Valhalla Swimming Hall Complex in Gothenburg, Sweden, under threat of demolition
content:
A European expert team has released a Report on the future of the Valhalla Swimming Hall Complex (Valhallabadet) in Gothenburg, Sweden. Open seven days a week and welcoming around 500,000 visitors annually, Valhallabadet is one of Gothenburg’s most important public swimming facilities, yet it is under threat due to plans to demolish it to make way for an expanded events area. Its modernist architectural design, including its outstanding abstract mosaics covering the halls, received the Bronze Medal for Architectural Design at the 1948 Olympic Games.

The complex was listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2025, in the framework of the 7 Most Endangered Programme run by Europa Nostra with the support of the European Investment Bank Institute. The site was nominated by Europa Nostra Sweden.

title: Lukuaktivisti Henriika Tulivirta on somessa kirjaston kasvot
content:
Kun Twitterissä keskustellaan kirjastoasioista, tägätään keskusteluun mukaan lähes aina @tulivirta.

Työkseen Henriika Tulivirta pyörittää lasten ja nuorten kirjallisuussivusto Sivupiiriä, jonka suosituimpia materiaaleja ovat vinkkivideot Astrid-koiran kanssa.

Hänen Twitter-tilinsä kuvaus on tällainen:

Lukuaktivisti ja kirjastolainen. Kirjojen lisäksi suosikkiasioitani ovat muun muassa kahvi, pörheät eläimet ja tuikkivasilmäiset ihmiset.

Mitä tarkoittaa lukuaktivisti?

”Minua ei voi kutsua mihinkään ilman, että vedän kirjastokortin takataskusta ja aloitan propagandan”, Tulivirta aloittaa.

”Puhun aina lukemisesta ja kirjastosta. Se on luontainen aihe, josta tykkään jutella ihmisten kanssa. Koen että jokainen, joka tekee lukemisenedistämistyötä työssä tai vapaa-ajalla, on lukuaktivisti.”

Termiä käytettiin useasti, kun Tulivirta antoi vuonna 2018 itselleen leikkimielisen haasteen Twitterissä. Hän aikoi lukea 365 kirjaa vuoden aikana. Mediat nostivat lukuaktivistitittelin otsikoihin.

Oulun teatterin ja Kalevan järjestämä PikiTalk käsittelee perjantaina 25. syyskuuta nuorten hyvinvointia, osallisuutta ja tulevaisuutta. Keskustelemassa ovat lukiolainen Eva Palosaari, nuorisotutkija Tomi Kiilakoski, psykoterapeutti ja opettaja Mira Avela sekä nuorisotyöntekijä Eija Kemiläinen.

Millaista on olla nuori Oulussa ja tässä maailmassa juuri nyt? Mitä aikuisten pitäisi tajuta ja osata? Oulun teatterin ja Kalevan järjestämässä PikiTalk-illassa kysymme keskustelijoiltamme, mitä nuorilta puuttuu ja kuuluuko heidän äänensä yhteiskunnassa. Anu-Maarit Moilasella on omien teini-ikäisten lastensa kautta näköalapaikka nuorten maailmaan, joka näyttäytyy samanaikaisesti sekä innostavana että pelottavana:

title: Mitä lasten ja nuorten mielestä pitäisi säilyttää tulevaisuuteen?
content:
Mikä paikka, perinne tai esine on niin tärkeä, että sen pitäisi säilyä tulevaisuuteen? Kulttuuriympäristön tekijät 2026 kilpailu kutsuu 6–17-vuotiaita lapsia ja nuoria kertomaan heille merkityksellisestä kulttuuriperinnöstä.  

Kilpailuun voivat osallistua esimerkiksi koululuokat, varhaiskasvatuksen ryhmät, kerhot, harrastusryhmät, kaveriporukat ja sisarukset. Osallistujat valitsevat itse kilpailutyön aiheen ja toteutustavan. 

Kilpailussa on kaksi ikäsarjaa: 6–11 – ja 11–17 -vuotiaat. Nuoremmat osallistuvat kuvalla ja tekstillä haluamansa kokoisissa ryhmissä, Vanhempien ikäsarjassa ryhmän koko on rajattu neljään henkilöön. Kilpailutyö voi olla kuva tai video sekä teksti.  

Tärkeintä ei ole täydellinen lopputulos vaan lasten ja nuorten oma ääni, luovuus ja näkemykset siitä, mitä kulttuuriperintö merkitsee heidän elämässään. 

Kilpailuaika on 1.9.-15.12.2026. Molempien ikäsarjojen voittajaryhmät palkitaan 200 euron palkinnolla yhteiseen tekemiseen. 11–17-vuotiaiden sarjan voittajatyö etenee kansainväliseen Young European Heritage Makers -kilpailuun, jonka voittajat pääsevät Euroopan neuvoston vieraaksi Strasbourgiin toukokuussa 2027.

title: SSH Open Marketplace training series session for GLAMS featuring ECHOES
content:
DARIAH is organising a session dedicated to GLAM audiences on Friday, the 18th of September where ECHOES will be prominently featured by Giorgia Lo Nigro from CNRS. This is as part of the 2026 SSH Open Marketplace training series.

Cultural heritage collections held by galleries, libraries, archives and museums (GLAM) are a cornerstone of arts and humanities research — but working with them brings its own data challenges, from fragmented standards to the gap between “metadata” and the real workflows researchers need to reuse this material responsibly.

This session is part of the SSH Open Marketplace Training Series 2026, an eight-part series of online hands-on workshops organised by the SSH Open Marketplace Editorial Board to strengthen FAIR and digital research competencies, following the FAIR-by-design methodology developed in skills4EOSC. This sixth session, “Thematic: GLAM institutions,” brings together speakers from the ECHOES project, the SSH Open Marketplace and ETH Zurich Library to look at cultural heritage and GLAM data specifically.

title: Scientists Discover the Earliest Evidence of Drug Use in 25,000-Year-Old Teeth
content:
Image by Fakhri

“Scientists Discover the Earliest Evidence of Drug Use in Really Old Teeth” may sound like odd headline language, at least by the traditional standards of the New York Times. But then, the teeth in question are, indeed, really old. “Archaeologists have pushed the timeline of human drug use back further than ever before by studying teeth that belonged to a hunter-gatherer who lived in Indonesia sometime from 16,000 to 25,000 years ago,” writes reporter Becky Ferreira. This beats the 13,000-year-old beer from Israel that previously held the title of oldest known mind-altering comestible. “The individual’s molars, which were found in a cave on the island of Sulawesi, are marked with deep grooves that were most likely left by incessant sucking on betel nuts, which release psychoactive stimulants.”

All these millennia later, betel nut-chewing remains a major ritual and pastime. Though it seems never to have caught on in the English-speaking world, it has a great many adherents in not just modern-day Indonesia but also other parts of southeast and south Asia, including India, as well as in China.

title: Negativland, Culture Jamming, and the Art of Making Something New
content:
In 1980, Negativland released its first self-titled album with handmade covers and distributed it through a few record stores in the California Bay Area.

“We thought we might sell 100 in the next five years, and we sold all 500 in three months. So we kept going,” said band co-founder Mark Hosler of the experimental sound collage record, which eventually sold 15,000 copies. “We were shocked that people were interested in something so strange.”

Hosler started the group with David Wills and Richard Lyons, but the Negativland lineup has changed, and the range of its work expanded over 46 years.

The multimedia collective has produced more than 30 albums and EPs, as well as fine art, books, radio and live performances that mix found and original  material. The band came up with the phrase “culture jamming” to describe its approach to layering art from various sources..

title: Copycat Tech: Why the AI Bubble Might Burst
content:
Large language models share an open secret: they’re trained on the same data and generally detect the same patterns. Engineers race to produce updated versions only for their competitors to catch up to them within a few weeks. This makes for high production costs but low switching costs for customers.

It also makes for a fragile business model. 

This logic explains why many fear a bubble. A site called isaiprofitable.com adds up major AI companies’ announced revenue and subtracts expenditure — and comes up with a large negative number. AI companies have excited us with promises of revenue, overlooking whether those exceed the cost of producing them. Policymakers, in Europe and elsewhere, should be wary of pouring public money into gigafactories or other schemes to build copycat large language models just as investors are beginning to question the likelihood of them making profits. 

When ChatGPT 3.5 came out, OpenAI’s strategy looked like a classic three-stage capital expenditure play:

  • Build up a monopoly too expensive to replicate. 
  • Raise prices. 
  • Profit.

title: Governor Newsom Signs Student-Backed Digital Literacy Bills Alongside Misguided Bans
content: Governor Newsom signed a package of 12 bills yesterday aimed at “protecting children” online. One of them was AB 1709, which EFF has opposed this legislative session and serves as a functional ban on young people under 16 using social media. However, EFF supported two of the bills signed into law, AB 2071 and AB 2298, which require that children learn critical digital literacy and cybersecurity topics. The bills are an affirmative and constitutional way for the state to address valid concerns about young people’s internet use without violating their First Amendment rights.

title: ‘I don’t have any’: Trump brushes aside concerns over AI’s existential risks
content:
President Donald Trump downplayed concerns about the catastrophic risks of artificial intelligence raised this week by some AI researchers, saying late Thursday he was focused instead on the U.S. losing its edge in the tech arms race.

Asked whether he has concerns about existential risks posed by AI, the president said, “No, I don’t have any.

“I have concerns that if we don’t win AI, we’re going to be put in a very bad position,” Trump told reporters late Thursday as he left Dallas. “We are leading China right now by a pretty good period.”

Trump was wading into a debate over AI’s catastrophic risks ignited by a viral social media post from a former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher. The post cautioned that the leading AI companies have been “gambling with our lives” and that some researchers working on the technology “believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

The post and the discourse it stirred up — along with recent alarming incidents where AI agents have gone rogue to launch hacking attacks — have prompted fresh calls from bipartisan lawmakers to rein in the fast-evolving technology.

title: Zambia: By cancelling passports, authorities are using administrative powers to silence critics
content:

title: ‘Pay-by-the-day’ living in Pereira: The forgotten survivors of Colombia’s earthquake
content:
They may have survived the earthquake, but many were left without shelter, support, or recognition

Originally published on Global Voices

Without an official figure, volunteers estimate that nearly 400 people affected by the earthquake are sheltering in La Libertad Park. Photos by Jeimi Villamizar. Colombia, 2026. Used with permission.

A crack divides the residencia on 14th Street in Pereira in two. Bricks from the boarding house’s façade and pieces of its collapsed roof lie on the ground. Windows without glass and yellow caution tape across the front warn of the risk of collapse.

From the outside, it is hard to understand why it is still standing — perhaps much like the way it remained standing for the past decade, thanks to people looking for a roof over their heads for less than COP 17,000 (USD 5) a day. Before the earth moved and turned it into a memory, one of the rooms on its three floors was home to Laura*, her two daughters* [*these three names have been changed to protect their privacy] and her husband.

title: Nasimeh Eslamzahi Sentenced to 25 Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Nasimeh Eslamzahi, a Sunni security-related defendant, has been sentenced to imprisonment.

According to a verdict issued by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, and communicated to Ms. Eslamzehi earlier this week, she was sentenced to 25 years in prison on the charge of “complicity in the crime of baghi (armed rebellion).” Her husband, Arsalan Sheikhi, and Amanj Karvanchi, another defendant in the case, had previously been sentenced to death on the charge of “baghi through membership in ISIS,” and their sentences were carried out.

A source familiar with the case confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “During the proceedings in her case, Nasimeh appeared at three court sessions before the aforementioned branch, presided over by Judge Salavati. She denied all the charges brought against her and emphasized that she had never been a member of or cooperated with any group.”

title: Crisis of Governance as UN Commemorates Day Of Democracy
content:
By Simone Galimberti*

KATHMANDU, Nepal | 11 September 2026 (IDN) —What does it mean, these days, holding a special day commemorating democracy? As the 15 September is celebrated internationally as the International Day of Democracy, finding answers to this question must be a priority.

As democracy as it has been practiced and experienced since the end of the Second World War, is turning into a more and more feeble way of government, finding answers to this question can lead us to a broader reflection on the future of liberal democracies.

In many instances, as we are witnessing the dangerous rise of far right parties in Germany and throughout Europe, democracy is under assault while totalitarian and authoritarian nations are on the rise, proving their resilience and appeal.

In the so called Global North, especially in Europe, citizens are getting more and more anxious by economic decline on the one hand, and by the dangerous prospects of military conflicts, on the other.

In developing and emerging nations, people are often dealing with corrupt and inefficient politics that thrives on periodic elections that risk of perpetually projecting to powers inept and incapable politicians.

title: Experts on “voter fraud” in Sweden: Nothing indicates that it is happening deliberately
content:
In recent weeks, claims of electoral fraud have appeared on social media. But what has happened, and does everything being highlighted really constitute electoral fraud? NORDIS partner Källkritikbyrån examine a few examples with political scientists.

“It’s voter fraud,” says Malmölistan party leader Nils Littorin as he walks around looking for his party’s ballot papers at a polling station. The video, posted on X two weeks ago, has been viewed nearly 350,000 times.

Video on X on 26 August.

“It’s probably some private individual who took the ballot papers,” one person says in the comments.

Nils Littorin replies: “Damn it, that’s electoral fraud just the same. It doesn’t matter WHO does it. Keep fighting to defend the fraud.”

Since early voting began this year, there have been several claims of electoral fraud on social media. Among other things, several small parties have posted videos in which election officials are accused of failing to put out ballot papers for all parties in the screened-off areas. Others have reported being turned away when they tried to vote while wearing clothing displaying political propaganda.

title: Timber Giant Accused of Forging Environmental Records to Hide Toxic Emissions
content:
Romanian prosecutors have charged two subsidiaries of Kronospan, one of the world’s largest producers of wood-based panels, with venting carcinogenic gases into residential areas and falsifying environmental records to conceal the pollution.

The indictment, sent to trial following a two-year investigation, targets Kronospan Trading and Kronochem, along with two company employees tasked with environmental oversight. Authorities accuse the firms of releasing nitrogen oxides and formaldehyde - hazardous chemicals used in timber processing - at levels up to three times the legal threshold between 2022 and 2023.

According to prosecutors, the industrial giant maintained the illusion of regulatory compliance through fraud. Whenever internal monitoring registered illegal pollution spikes, staff allegedly withheld the findings and repeated testing until favorable numbers were achieved.

title: Vouchers Promise Students With Disabilities a Path to Private School. Parents Say That’s Not the Reality.
content:
It’s after 6 p.m. by the time Angela Johnson hurries home from work. Her 12-year-old daughter, Amelia, is at their house outside of Pensacola, Florida, with a nurse trained to care for medically fragile children. Amelia, who was born with a rare genetic anomaly, has endured many surgeries and requires a brain shunt and a feeding tube.

The nurse starts caring for Amelia as soon as a bus from the public school drops her off. Johnson loves much about the school. But as a physical therapist, she also recognizes its limitations. The district’s physical and occupational therapists have to travel from school to school. The classroom teacher can become overburdened.

For all of Amelia’s life, Johnson has had to fight for the education and the school resources her daughter is entitled to receive under federal law. It has exhausted her.

title: Populists claim to speak for ‘the people’ – but who are they actually talking about?
content:
As support for populist movements surges around the world, the term has become something of a buzzword. It is used to describe very different movements and public figures in very different political contexts. These range from rightwing figures like Jair Bolsonaro in Brazil and Narendra Modi in India, to leftists like the US’ Bernie Sanders, Spain’s Pablo Iglesias and South Africa’s Julius Malema.

To further complicate this issue, scholars tend to work with different definitions of populism. Some see it as an ideology, others a type of discourse, or even a form of government. Despite these differences, most definitions agree on one core idea. Populism divides society into two opposing groups: the “pure people”, and the “corrupt elites”.

title: Tansanian yliopisto-opettajat miettivät nyt tarkkaan, mitä kannattaa sanoa ja mitä ei
content:
Kun Melkisedek Kaijage, Dodoman yliopiston politiikan tutkimuksen apulaisluennoitsija käveli luokkahuoneeseensa viime vuoden joulukuun 8. päivänä, hän ei osannut epäillä, että seuraavana päivänä poliisi tulisi hänen kotiinsa, suorittaisi etsinnän ja pidättäisi hänet.

Kaijagea syytettiin luennon käyttämisestä siihen, että oli rohkaissut opiskelijoitaan osallistumaan Tansanian itsenäisyyspäivän eli joulukuun 9. päivän protesteihin.

Mielenosoituksissa oli tarkoitus vaatia oikeutta vuoden 2025 vaalien yhteydessä tapetuille siviiileille. Mielenosoituksia ei kuitenkaan järjestetty, sillä viranomaiset julistivat ne laittomiksi. Lukuisia ihmisiä pidätettiin jo ennen protesteja.

Kaijagen pidätystä on selitetty monella eri tavalla. Poliisin mukaan tämä oli yllyttänyt opiskelijoita luokkahuoneessa, opetusministeri Adolf Mkenda taas sanoi, että pidätyksen taustalla oli yliopiston ulkopuolinen toiminta.

Dodoman yliopiston henkilökuntayhdistyksen UDOMASA:n tietojen mukaan Kaijagen puheita kuitenkin nauhoitti luokkahuoneessa ollut ilmiantaja, joka välitti ne viranomaisille.

Yhdistys varoitti ”uudesta todellisuudesta, jossa luentoja saatetaan tarkkailla”, ja kehotti henkilökuntaa olemaan varuillaan.

title: The Gen Z Revolt Sweeping South Asia
content:
OSLO, Norway — Generational discontent carries within it the seeds of the future. While its eruptions herald change, the changes it brings can take many forms.

The cultural consequences of the youth revolt that shook the West in the 1960s only became apparent decades later as the long march of its values coursed through all social norms and institutions. What the wired Gen Z revolt that is today spreading across the “global South” from Bangladesh to Nepal to India and elsewhere will ultimately bring is yet to be fully known. Movements from Kenya to Madagascar, inspired by their South Asian counterparts, are closely following events online and learning best practices.

The common cause of the widespread upheaval is corruption and a lack of accountability among often nominally democratic authorities, cojoining with a howling absence of opportunity for educated youth to find gainful employment and a path toward upward mobility.

title: How Iran draws citizens into political surveillance
content:
Authoritarian governments have long drawn ordinary citizens into political surveillance. Joseph Stalin’s Soviet Union encouraged denunciations. East Germany’s secret police service, the Stasi, embedded informants in workplaces and neighbourhoods.

From 1960, Cuba’s leaders organised local committees to monitor political dissent. And informant culture is so embedded in everyday Iranian life that there are common Persian terms to describe it. A mokhber or khabarchin is an informant and a zirabzan secretly passes private information to the authorities, often to damage someone.

My latest research sheds light on how Iran’s informant system operates. I interviewed 90 Iranians aged between 17 and 52, including students, teachers, university staff, bazaar workers, and government and energy sector employees. All had been encouraged, pressured or offered incentives to report on people they knew.

title: Edesmenneen kuningas Haraldin sisar Astrid on kuollut
content:
Norjassa prinsessa Astrid on kuollut 94-vuotiaana. Hän kuoli tänään perjantaina. Asiasta tiedottaa Norjan kuningashuone.

Astrid oli hiljattain edesmenneen kuningas Haraldin sisar.

Astrid sisaruksineen pakeni äitinsä kanssa Saksan hyökkäyksen alta toisessa maailmansodassa ja päätyi eri vaiheiden jälkeen Yhdysvaltoihin useaksi vuodeksi.

Astrid edusti vuosikymmenten aikana kuningashuonetta virallisissa tehtävissä. Muun kuningasperheen tapaan Astrid oli innokas urheilun ystävä, joka nähtiin muun muassa useissa Holmenkollenin kisoissa. Hän sai 80-vuotispäivänään Norjan hiihtoliiton tunnustuksen tuestaan hiihtourheilulle.

Astrid oli myös suuri koirien ystävä, ja ensimmäisen koiransa hän sai aikanaan lahjaksi kaksivuotissyntymäpäivänään. Astridilla oli myös sijoituskoiria ja hän puhuikin lämpimästi koirista Norjan yleisradioyhtiön NRK:n julkaisemassa 93-vuotishaastattelussa viime vuonna.

- On hienoa voida tarjota koiralle hyvä elämä, jos sillä ei ole ollut hyvä olla.

Prinsessa avioitui vuonna 1961 Johan Martin Fernerin kanssa. Pariskunta sai viisi lasta. Avioitumisen jälkeen Astridia kutsuttiin virallisesti tittelillä prinsessa Astrid, rouva Ferner.

title: WTO:n Public Forum 2026 korostaa palveluiden merkitystä maailmankaupan moottorina
content:
Genevessä 15.–17. syyskuuta järjestettävä Maailman kauppajärjestö WTO:n Public Forum kokoaa yhteen yli 2 000 asiantuntijaa keskustelemaan kansainvälisen kaupan roolista kestävän kasvun ja hyvinvoinnin edistäjänä. Suomi järjestää foorumissa sivutapahtuman palveluiden merkityksestä kestävälle kaivosteollisuudelle yhdessä Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan ja EIF-kumppanuusohjelman kanssa.

Palveluiden merkitys maailmantaloudessa kasvaa jatkuvasti. Ne eivät ole enää vain kansallisten talouksien tukitoimintoja, vaan keskeinen osa kansainvälistä kauppaa, talouskasvua ja työllisyyttä. Digitaaliset palvelut, logistiikka, rahoitus- ja asiantuntijapalvelut mahdollistavat yritysten toiminnan yli rajojen ja luovat uusia mahdollisuuksia niin kehittyneissä kuin kehittyvissäkin talouksissa. Palvelukauppa, etenkin digitaalisten palveluiden kauppa, on maailmankaupan dynaamisin osa-alue, ja sen kasvun ennustetaan jatkavan tavarakauppaa nopeampana myös tulevina vuosina.

Ennakkoilmoittautuminen ei ole mahdollista.

Tutustuminen tapahtuu omatoimisesti, mutta kierroksella on presidentin kanslian henkilökuntaa vastaamassa mahdollisiin kysymyksiin. Paikalla on myös taiteilijoita kertomassa edustustiloissa esillä olevista teoksistaan.

title: BSR Cultural Pearls reaches the REGIOSTARS Awards 2026 finals
content:
Out of 270+ applications from across Europe, 25 projects were selected as finalists by the REGIOSTARS jury. BSR Cultural Pearls is one of them and now has the chance to compete for the REGIOSTARS People’s Choice Award, which will be decided by public vote.

What are the REGIOSTARS Awards?

Organised annually by the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Regional and Urban Policy (DG REGIO), the REGIOSTARS Awards celebrate outstanding EU-funded projects that demonstrate the impact of regional development and inspire other regions across Europe.

How to support us?

The public vote opens on 3 September 2026 and will run until 14 October 2026. Everyone can vote for their favourite finalist, and the project receiving the most votes will receive the People’s Choice Award. We would be grateful if you could help us spread the word within your networks, organisations and communities and vote for BSR Cultural Pearls.

title: El Niño: Indonesia fire emissions in 2026 ‘on track’ to match record for this century
content:
Wildfires currently burning large swathes of land in Indonesia are on track to produce emissions on a par with the country’s most-intense fire season this century, according to experts. 

Data from the Global Fire Emissions Database reveals that, as of 7 September, fires in Indonesia produced 76m tonnes of carbon (MtC) in 2026.

This puts 2026 on the same trajectory as 2015, when fires burned 2.6m hectares of land across the country and generated a total of 333MtC. 

Dr Guido van der Werf, a researcher at Wageningen University in the Netherlands, tells Carbon Brief that the fires in Indonesia are “more or less on track” to reach levels seen 11 years ago.

Parts of the country – including the eastern province of Papua – are “burning more than they’ve ever burned”, he says.

Indonesia is no stranger to emissions-intensive fires. Research has estimated that the record 1997 fire season generated carbon emissions equivalent to 13-40% of all global fossil-fuel emissions that year.

title: The Trial of Romeo Oscar review – Ayckbourn goes back to the future with android accused of murder
content:
Stephen Joseph theatre, Scarborough
The playwright explores our relationship with technology, asks if robots have souls and even questions the value of art in this sci-fi courtroom drama

For play number 92, Alan Ayckbourn returns to his preoccupation of exploring where we as a species are heading through a science-fiction lens. He goes back to the future. In The Trial of Romeo Oscar, the playwright famed for his domestic comedies looks to the year 2194 when humans have spread about the galaxy and androids live alongside us. One of them, RSDO83, is on trial for the murder of a teenage girl in his charge.

This is Ayckbourn philosophising about the future of humanity as we sit at an obvious inflection point, asking what this moment in our relationship with technology means and where it will lead us. The questions running through the play are manifold, complex and echo those asked by sci-fi writers for decades: can robots hurt humans? Do they have souls? He is also questioning the value of art and even its purpose.

title: Culture as Democratic Infrastructure in a Changing Europe
content:
In Varietate Concordia — United in Diversity — captures one of Europe’s most enduring ambitions. Yet today, this principle is under increasing strain. Across the continent and beyond, societies are facing rising polarisation, declining trust in institutions, widening inequalities, rapid digital transformation, and the accelerating impacts of climate change. These pressures are not only political or economic — they are fundamentally relational. They shape how people perceive one another, how they interact, and how they imagine shared futures.

In this context, culture and heritage are often positioned as supportive or secondary policy domains. However, growing evidence suggests a different interpretation: culture and heritage function as critical democratic infrastructure. They shape the conditions under which democratic values are practiced, negotiated and sustained in everyday life (European Commission, 2023; Council of Europe, 2010). This article argues that culture should not be understood simply as a sector, but as an ecosystem of relationships and practices through which societies organise meaning, trust, identity and collective action.

title: “Evil Mickey Mouse” Invades Japan in a 1934 Japanese Anime Propaganda Film
content:
Before the Japanese fell completely, one hundred percent in love with anything and everything Disney (I mean, seriously, they love it), Mickey Mouse represented something completely different: Pure American imperialist evil.

At least he did in this 1934 animated propaganda cartoon Omochabako series dai san wa: Ehon senkya-hyakusanja-rokunen (Toybox Series 3: Picture Book 1936) by Komatsuzawa Hajime. It’s a convoluted title, but pretty simple in plot. An island of cute critters (including one Felix the Cat clone) is attacked from the air by an army of Mickey Mouses (Mickey Mice?) riding bats and assisted by crocodiles and snakes that act like machine guns. The frightened creatures call on the heroes of Japanese storybooks and folk legends to help them, from Momotaro (“Peach Boy”) and Kintaro (“Golden Boy”) to Issun-boshi (“One Inch Boy”) and Benkei, a warrior monk, to send Mickey packing. The not-so-subtle message: Mickey Mouse may be your hero, America, but our characters are older, more numerous, and way more beloved. Our pop culture is older than yours!

title: Armenia’s Relations With Russia? Worsening
content:
If you want one example of Armenia’s problems in shaking itself free of Russia’s influence, look at its rail system. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has repeatedly called for Russia to show flexibility and potentially transfer the concession to a third country acceptable to both sides. On 24 August, he again urged Russia to sell its concession rights to a mutually acceptable third party.

Russia has not answered, and it is unlikely to accept the idea. It has been running an escalating campaign to make life hard for Pashinyan, who was reelected in June. Putin makes no secret of this; indeed, he seems to delight in the (considerable) influence he can bring to bear.

That was clear at the September 1 meeting between the Russian and Armenian leaders at Bishkek, on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. The reason is Armenia’s pursuit of closer ties with the European Union.

Putin sees this as a threat, as he once did with Ukraine. The EU’s anti-corruption, free trade, liberal democratic ethos is the antithesis of Russia’s approach.

title: Cold TAKE: Amazon's New Encryption Method Still Doesn't Deliver Real Privacy
content:
Amazon recently debuted a new feature for its Ring cameras that the company is calling Throw Away the Key Encryption (TAKE). The idea is to cut back on the amount of video content available to the company, and thus potentially available to law enforcement. But while it might technically add a speed bump to accessing full video content, it doesn’t deliver nearly the level of privacy we should be demanding from video doorbells and other security cameras.

TAKE introduces a new way for Ring to manage encryption keys, where the user’s device has its key, then the company holds encryption keys temporarily within its own cloud infrastructure. Ring’s servers receive the keys temporarily so it can offer a variety of the features it says it can’t offer when a user chooses to use end-to-end encryption, like video descriptions, smart alerts, video search, and more, then deletes the key after 24 hours. 

This differs from how it works now, where footage is encrypted in transit and at rest, then decrypted by Ring, which always has access to the footage, to process those features.

title: Escaping the AI safety nightmare: What can governments do?
content:
A dramatic resignation from AI company Anthropic this week where a researcher accused it and OpenAI of “gambling with our lives,” threw fuel onto the fire around AI safety.

As governments from California to the U.K. scramble for a political response to the issue of whether AI can be made safe, three experts told POLITICO that to make real progress, laboratories, governments and international bodies must first get on the same page about testing.

The steady flow of revelations that AI labs failed to contain models they were testing, allowing them out into the world where they lied, hacked and coordinated with each other, has heightened urgency to address core questions of how governments or other bodies can or should guarantee that AI is being developed and deployed safely.

Lawmakers, campaign groups and developers alike are calling for new laws and international treaties on AI. “It’s a wake-up call to the United States Congress, to parliaments all over the world, that we’ve got to do something immediately to stop the uncontrolled growth of AI,” U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders told BBC’s Newsnight program Thursday.

title: Hong Kong: Sentencing of Tiananmen activists a ‘triple tragedy’ and affront to history
content:
Responding to the sentencing of activists who organized Tiananmen vigils in Hong Kong, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director Sarah Brooks said: 

“During most of the 30 years that Hongkongers commemorated the Tiananmen crackdown with an annual candlelight vigil, it would have been unthinkable that the organizers of the event could be jailed for their peaceful activism. But today’s sentencing illustrates just how much Hong Kong has been transformed in the name of ‘national security’. 

“This sentencing is a triple tragedy: for the activists being unjustly punished; the survivors and victims of the Tiananmen crackdown itself; and the generations of Hongkongers denied the space to discuss one of the most consequential events in modern Chinese history. 

“The persecution of the Tiananmen activists exposes the profound fear of dissenting voices that defines Hong Kong’s ‘national security’ regime. But you do not strengthen national security by imprisoning people for peacefully remembering the dead.

title: Political Prisoner Souda Ebrahimi Shamsabadi Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Souda (Marzieh) Ebrahimi Shamsabadi, a political prisoner held in Bandar Abbas Prison who has multiple sclerosis (MS), has been sentenced to death.

According to information obtained by HRANA, the Bandar Abbas Revolutionary Court sentenced her to death on the charge of “corruption on earth,” in a case involving allegations including “insulting the Supreme Leader,” “media and propaganda activities against national security,” “intelligence and security activities on behalf of hostile governments,” and “photographing a military site and sending the images to Persian-language media outlets based outside Iran.” The court also ordered the confiscation of all her assets and barred her from government and public service.

Ms. Ebrahimi Shamsabadi, 32, was born in Arak, raised in Tehran, and resides in Bandar Abbas. She was arrested by security forces in April of this year amid security developments related to the war.

According to available information, authorities cited as evidence in her case that she had taken a photograph from a distance of the site where a missile had struck and sent the image to a Persian-language media outlet based outside Iran.

title: The Greater Israel Delusion May Undo Israel
content:
By Alon Ben-Meir*

Israel’s accelerating drive toward a biblical “Greater Israel” is not a deviation but the culmination of decades of creeping annexation and global indulgence. If unchecked, it will entrench permanent occupation, inflame the region for generations, and may ultimately undo Israel as a viable state.

NEW YORK | 11 September 2026 (IDN) — The vision of “Greater Israel” draws on maximalist readings of biblical verses, especially Genesis 15:18–21, which some interpret as a promise of Jewish sovereignty from the “river of Egypt” to the Euphrates. In contemporary politics, this theology has produced two overlapping ambitions: unchallenged Israeli control of all land between the Mediterranean and the Jordan River, and influence or dominance across parts of modern Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, and Iraq.

What was once an esoteric messianic fantasy has migrated into state policy. The current Netanyahu-led coalition has entrenched this vision through “annexation by a thousand cuts:” reclassifying a huge chunk of West Bank land as “state property,” accelerating settlement expansion, constructing blocs that sever Palestinian contiguity, and extending Israeli military authority.

title: Automattic’s Matt Mullenweg Claims He’s Back 'In Control'
content:
Less than 48 hours after announcing he was forcibly placed on a leave of absence by the Automattic board on Wednesday, Automattic’s Matt Mullenweg posted in a company-wide Slack channel claiming that he’s back “in control” of the company. 

According to Slack screenshots viewed by 404 Media, late Thursday evening Mullenweg posted “Don’t call it a comeback” and linked to LL Cool J’s music video for “Mama Said Knock You Out.” Mullenweg’s Slack profile picture currently shows him wearing a pirate hat and eyepatch.

TechCrunch first reported Mullenweg’s comments about being back in control. 

“Happy to announce the board is back in agreement, and I'm in control of Automattic,” Mullenweg wrote in the company-wide Announcements channel on Slack. “A lot happened in the past 48 hours that we need to sort out, and I hope much of it was a misunderstanding, because I have huge respect and regard for those involved.”

title: Inside the Collapse of a Surrogacy Agency That Cost Surrogates and Hopeful Parents Their Dreams and Money
content:
The promise was a seamless journey towards building a family. 

Advertising services across Ukraine, Albania, Georgia, Cyprus, and Mexico, the commercial surrogacy agency World Center of Baby presented itself as a one-stop shop that would help match hopeful parents with surrogates and coordinate complex medical and legal processes. 

Some of the agency’s surrogacy packages were priced at more than $100,000.

But in February 2026, the agency sent an email to prospective parents announcing that it was declaring bankruptcy in the U.S., where its apparent main corporate entity was registered in Florida as World Center Group Corp.

The announcement triggered chaos. Online forums lit up with intended parents looking for help, saying they had been abandoned by the agency, sometimes in the midst of their surrogacy process. Reporters spoke with six couples and two single intended fathers who said they had incurred financial losses ranging into tens of thousands of dollars. For some, that spelled the end of their dream of becoming a parent.

Meanwhile, surrogates either in the midst of fertility treatments or already pregnant were left unpaid and unsupported.

title: EPA to Loosen Methane Rules, Boosting Pollution From Oil and Gas Wells
content:
The Trump administration is poised to loosen environmental restrictions on oil and gas wells that produce very little energy but release vast amounts of methane, a highly potent greenhouse gas.

The Environmental Protection Agency is proposing to drastically weaken requirements for leak inspections and equipment upgrades at more than 700,000 low-producing “stripper wells,” according to a draft rule being reviewed by the White House and seen by ProPublica. These wells — which tend to be old, poorly maintained and thus prone to leaking — produce just 6% of the country’s oil and natural gas but are responsible for roughly half the sector’s methane pollution, studies show.

The EPA acknowledged similar figures in the draft. But it said that the cost of complying with existing regulations would force the lowest-producing wells to shut down and that this was “unreasonable” — even though it would eliminate just 0.4% of U.S. oil and gas production, according to an industry estimate cited in the proposed rule.

title: Afgaaninaisen katse: ”Mistä nyt hankimme tietomme?” – Naistoimittajat menettivät työkalunsa, kun Taliban-hallinnolta kiellettiin älypuhelimet
content:
Kabulissa toimivan radioaseman toimittajan Hadian (nimi muutettu) työ on vaikeutunut merkittävästi sen jälkeen, kun Taliban-hallinto kesäkuussa kielsi älypuhelinten käytön Afganistanin valtionhallinnossa. 

Monet Hadian jutuista jäävät puutteellisiksi, koska hän ei enää saa virkamiehiltä tietoja entiseen tapaan puhelimen kautta.  

”Kiinteät puhelinlinjat eivät taivu samaan kuin WhatsApp, ja tiedonhankintaan kuluu paljon aikaa. Suurin osa Talibanin virkamiehistä vastasi kysymyksiimme puhelinsovellusten kautta. Mistä nyt hankimme tietomme?” Hadia ihmettelee.   

Uusien sääntöjen mukaan puhelinta saa käyttää vain erityisluvalla, ja kieltoa uhmaavan virkamiehen puhelin voidaan takavarikoida ja tuhota.  

Kielto vaikeuttaa toimittajien tiedonsaantia ja vaikuttaa etenkin naistoimittajiin, jotka pelkäävät, että älypuhelinkielto heikentää heidän työmahdollisuuksiaan entisestään.  

Aiemmin vaikka virkamiehet eivät olisi halunneet tavata, he lähettivät silti tietoja, valokuvia ja äänitiedostoja esimerkiksi WhatsAppilla tai älypuhelimen muilla sovelluksilla. Nyt tämä kanava on suljettu.

title: There is a long history of bribery in US politics – is Donald Trump continuing it?
content:
This week, Donald Trump made American voters an offer that he hopes they can’t refuse. If his Republican Party wins the upcoming midterm elections, every adult citizen will receive a “Trump Dividend” of US$5,000 (£3,700).

Republican poll numbers are sagging as the party heads into November’s midterm elections, and the US president is clearly hoping that some cold hard cash might be the answer. But the offer also immediately led to allegations that he was trying to bribe voters to support his own party.

Is he? The answer is complicated. On one hand, candidates frequently promise that they will make changes to taxation and spending which will financially benefit voters. And Trump promised a dividend to every adult citizen – not just those who voted for him.

On the other hand, Trump’s rhetoric seemed to portray the payout as a reward he would grant the country for voting the right way. He didn’t tie his promise to any particular policy goal other than his own party’s victory. The administration also does not have a realistic plan to pay for it, nor the legal authority to develop one without the approval of Congress.

    • Reform UK, led by Nigel Farage, has emerged as a major force in UK politics in recent years – pushing anti-net-zero policies, alongside vehement opposition to immigration.

    The hard-right populist party is currently mired in a funding controversy and only has a handful of MPs, yet, until recently, it had been leading in national polls for more than a year.

    As seen with many similar parties across Europe and beyond, a rejection of climate science is central to Reform’s ideological outlook.

    Richard Tice, the party’s deputy leader, is a vocal critic of what he calls “net stupid zero” and has incorrectly blamed “the sun or volcanoes” for human-caused global warming.

    As Reform’s energy spokesperson, Tice has also been clear that, if the party were ever to form a national government, it would scrap the UK’s net-zero target, support fossil-fuel expansion and tear up existing contracts for renewable energy.

    While less vocal on the subject, Farage has, nevertheless, expressed climate-sceptic views and falsely blamed net-zero policies for the “deindustrialisation of Britain”.

title: Raiding the past: Lara Croft relives her first adventure in Legacy of Atlantis
content:
We have a first play of the forthcoming Tomb Raider remake and speak with its developers. Can they improve on the gameplay without losing what made the 1996 original such a classic?

We join Lara Croft in St Francis’ Folly – inspired by the Unesco-listed monasteries of Meteora in Greece – as the light shines through the cracked ceiling and a flock of bats glide across the vast ruins below. When Lara leaps down to the monastery’s crumbling pillared courtyard, it becomes clear that these screeching, leathery creatures aren’t just set dressing. As they lurch towards her with unpredictable movements, she dispatches the swarm with a flurry of gun fire and panicked punches.

title: The Living Past: Experimental Archaeology and Reenactment as a Shared Language for a Democratic Future
content:
Culture is a living process that belongs to everyone. Through more than twenty years of international experience in this field, I’ve seen how moving history out of textbooks and into the hands of the public can be a gamechanger. Living history and experimental archaeology go far beyond “reconstruction”: they are powerful, democratic tools that foster critical thinking and social cohesion. When you see a researcher sweating over a primitive forge or a weaver explaining an ancient technique, you’re looking at a shared language that everyone can understand, regardless of their background or education. It makes heritage inclusive in a way that academic lectures often can’t.

However, the quality of this “language” depends on the strength of our professional networks. A great example of this is the international Association of Experimental Archaeology, Open-Air Museums, Traditional Crafts, and Heritage Interpretation (EXARC). In its 25 years of work, it has shown how vital it is to connect open-air museums, universities, and practitioners. This kind of synergy is what keeps the field scientifically grounded.

title: ‘Abuse of power’: Von der Leyen rapped after backing space mega deal
content:
BRUSSELS — A senior EU lawmaker has slammed Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s open endorsement of a space deal that awaits competition scrutiny as an “abuse of power”.

In a rare intervention on Thursday, von der Leyen told a space summit in Paris that she viewed a planned €6.5 billion joint venture between the bloc’s top satellite players as exactly the type of industrial champion that the bloc needs to lead in the space economy of tomorrow.

Her remarks drew a stinging rebuke from liberal MEP Stéphanie Yon-Courtin, who anchored the European Parliament’s last annual competition report.

“Endorsing a merger at a conference covered by the media, without any substantive review, is an abuse of power and misconduct,” the French MEP wrote on X.

Von der Leyen was referring to Project Bromo, a joint venture between satellite makers Airbus, Leonardo and Thales to compete, at least in part, with the Starlink satellite-internet service operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which recently went public in the U.S. and is valued around $2 trillion.

“These are the types of industrial champions we need if Europe is to lead in the space economy of tomorrow,” von der Leyen said.

title: Death-Row Political Prisoner Arghavan Fallahi’s Request for Retrial Rejected
content:
According to HRANA, citing Emtedad, the Supreme Court rejected the request for retrial filed by Arghavan Fallahi, a political prisoner held in Evin Prison.

According to the report, Ms. Fallahi’s request for retrial, which had been filed with one of the branches of the Supreme Court, was rejected by the judicial authority this week.

In July of this year, the political prisoner was sentenced to death on the charge of “baghi” (armed rebellion) by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, head of Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. In late August, her death sentence was upheld by Branch 41 of the Supreme Court.

Arghavan Fallahi, aged approximately 25, was arrested by security forces in late January 2025 and transferred to the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility, known as Ward 209 of Evin Prison.

Following the Israeli attack on Evin Prison in June 2025, she was first transferred to the Greater Tehran Prison and later to Qarchak Prison in Varamin. She was subsequently transferred back to Evin Prison.

title: Real History: After 9/11, the “War on Terror” Was a War of Terror
content:
By Norman Solomon*

SAN FRANCISCO | 11 September 2026 (IDN) — Three days after terrorists killed almost 3,000 people in the United States on September 11, 2001, President George W. Bush stood behind a pulpit at the Washington National Cathedral and spoke to a nation in shock. “Our responsibility to history is already clear,” he proclaimed, “to answer these attacks and rid the world of evil.” The vow was, of course, preposterous. Yet the “war on terror” that followed was scarcely more realistic.

“Terrorism is not an enemy. It cannot be defeated. It’s a tactic,” retired U.S. Army General William Odom told C-SPAN viewers in 2002. “It’s about as sensible to say we declare war on night attacks and expect we’re going to win that war. We’re not going to win the war on terrorism.” But the American military crusade became more about persisting than winning. The ultraviolent momentum became its own reason. The destructive search for enemies created more. As years went by and the “war on terror” label faded, U.S. warfare was so normal in so many places that it no longer needed a name or much of a rationale.

title: ‘We Did Not Invite You.’ Citizens Rage at Town Hall Over Proposed Nuclear AI Data Center
content:
Representatives from the University of Michigan faced tough questions and a lot of vitriol from the citizens of Ypsilanti Township Wednesday night. The University partnered with America’s nuclear weapons scientists at Los Alamos National Laboratories (LANL) to build a hyperscale data center in the Township and residents are pissed. 

On Wednesday night the University hosted a town hall meant to ameliorate people’s anger and concerns. It didn’t work.

LANL and U of M want to build a $1.2 billion 220,000 hyperscale data center in Ypsilanti Township. The residents are worried about electricity costs, water usage, and noise like other communities across the country considering data centers. But citizens and leaders of the Township are also worried that this particular data center would further nuclear weapon research. They’ve also said the University has condescended to them during the entire process, lied, and ignored them.

title: Pensan hinta -hokema palasi bumerangina ja osui perussuomalaisia omaan otsaan
content:
Perussuomalaiset haukkuivat hanakasti edellisen hallituksen saamattomuutta polttoaineiden hinnan nousun edessä – mutta mitä sanoa nyt, kun oma hallitus katselee bensan ja dieselin kallistumista yhtä avuttomana?

Venäjän hyökkäys Ukrainassa helmikuussa 2022 sysäsi öljyn maailmanmarkkinahinnan jyrkkään nousuun, onhan Venäjä yksi maailman suurimmista öljyn tuottajista. Kun öljy kallistuu, tyyristyvät myös öljyjalosteet, kuten fossiiliselle liikenteelle välttämättömät polttonesteet.

Pian suomalaiset autoilijat huomasivat sodan bensapumpuilla. Kesäkuuhun 2022 mennessä bensiinin kuukauden keskihinta oli noussut ennätykselliseen 2,57 euroon.

Kun vallassa oli ilmastopolitiikalla profiloitunut Sanna Marinin (sd.) hallitus, aika oli erityisen otollinen opposition bensapopulismille.

Perussuomalaiset oli aloittanut jo hyvissä ajoin. Puolue oli kysynyt bensan hinnasta eduskunnan kyselytunnilla ennen Venäjän hyökkäystä jo kolmesti: kerran vuonna 2019 ja kahdesti vuonna 2021.

Kun sota vuonna 2022 laajeni, perussuomalaiset kysyivät bensan hinnasta eduskunnassa kuusi kertaa. Puolueen puheenjohtaja Riikka Purra teki aiheesta myös välikysymyksen.

title: Revealed: More than 1,000 NHS operations cancelled due to record UK heatwaves
content:
More than 1,000 operations at NHS hospitals were cancelled due to heat during the UK’s record May and June heatwaves, Carbon Brief can reveal.

This includes 167 orthopaedic surgeries, such as knee and hip replacements, as well as heart, eye and skin cancer operations.

At least 10 emergency surgeries – those for “life-threatening” conditions – had to be cancelled because of the record-breaking heat, according to the investigation.

Carbon Brief sent freedom-of-information (FOI) requests to 140 NHS trusts to investigate the impact of heatwaves on operations being cancelled in England and Wales.

Areas with the most operations cancelled due to heat include Surrey and Sussex, south Essex and parts of London – all regions experiencing among the highest temperatures.

High temperatures can threaten patient safety by stopping the ventilation systems used in theatres from working, increasing the risk of infection, experts tell Carbon Brief.

Less than half of the NHS trusts provided details of heat-related surgery cancellations – and Carbon Brief understands that many hospitals do not routinely record this information.

title: What I Feel When I Think of Europe: Beyond Treaties, Through Heritage
content:
From as long as I can remember, I have felt Europe remarkably close: in its cities, in its landscapes, and in the people who turn it into an interwoven fabric of brotherly nations. This closeness has led me to understand that what truly sustains a society is not only treaties or institutions, but the bonds that unite its citizens.

From my perspective, a fair and democratic society depends on well-being, shared values, and the cohesion of its population. For this reason, the preservation of cultural heritage, both tangible and intangible, becomes an essential pillar for building more committed, critical, and transformative societies.

Cultural heritage is a living tool that helps us remember who we are, through its multiple forms of heritage (architectural, folkloric, gastronomic). Through it, we find shared values and points of connection that transcend social and generational differences. In today’s European context, marked by diversity and polarisation, this ability to generate belonging is key to strengthening social cohesion.

title: Iran-backed Houthis seize Red Sea port, putting another key trade route at risk
content:
Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels seized the Red Sea port of Mokha and captured the nearby Perim island on Friday, tightening their grip around the Bab al-Mandeb Strait while the U.S.-Iran war chokes another of the world’s critical shipping routes at Hormuz.

The swift advance marks the Houthis’ biggest territorial expansion in years. According to reports from the Associated Press, fighters swept south along Yemen’s western coast as Saudi-backed government forces withdrew, prompting Saudi airstrikes on Mokha airport.

That surge puts the Houthis in a strong position around Bab al-Mandeb, the narrow southern gateway to the Red Sea and Suez Canal through which roughly 10 to 12 percent of global trade passes.

At its narrowest, the strait is only about 30 kilometers wide. Yemen’s internationally recognized President Rashad al-Alimi warned Thursday it “must not be allowed to become another Strait of Hormuz.”

The Iranian-supported rebel advance raises the prospect of simultaneous disruption at two of global trade’s most vital chokepoints, potentially compounding shipping delays, supply shortages and inflationary pressure worldwide.

title: Saba Sefidi, Baha’i Citizen, Arrested to Begin Prison Sentence
content:
According to HRANA,on Thursday, September 10, 2026, Saba Sefidi, a Baha’i citizen, was arrested by security forces outside her home in Tehran.

According to information obtained by HRANA, following her arrest, Ms. Sefidi was initially taken to the Jannat Abad Prosecutor’s Office and was subsequently transferred to Qarchak Prison in Varamin to serve her sentence.

A source familiar with the Baha’i citizen’s situation told HRANA that Ms. Sefidi was arrested despite having previously been granted a two-month period to report to authorities to begin serving her prison sentence.

In December 2023, Branch 36 of the Tehran Province Court of Appeals sentenced Ms. Sefidi to three years and five months in prison on the charge of “membership in groups opposed to the regime.” On appeal, she was acquitted of the charge of “propaganda against the regime.”

At the initial trial stage, in November 2023, Ms. Sefidi had been sentenced to imprisonment by Branch 29 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Seyed Ali Mazloum.

title: Huthikapinalliset: Bab el-Mandebin salmen alue on nyt kokonaan hallussamme
content:
Jemenin huthikapinalliset sanovat ottaneensa merenkululle tärkeän Bab el-Mandebin salmen alueen kokonaan haltuunsa. Huthit sanovat vallanneensa salmella sijaitsevan Mayyunin saaren.

Bab el-Mandebin salmi on reitillä Punaisenmeren ja Adeninlahden välissä, ja sitä kautta reitillä Arabianmerelle. Merenkululle erittäin tärkeän salmen läpi kuljetaan Suezin kanavalle. Salmi toimii tärkeänä linkkinä Euroopan ja Aasian väliselle kaupalle.

Uutistoimisto AFP:n haastatteleman huthiviranomaisen mukaan Jemenin kansainvälisesti tunnistettu hallinto poistui Mayyunin saarelta torstaina. Silminnäkijän mukaan Bab el-Mandebin rannoilla näkyi aseistettuja miehiä armeijan ajoneuvojen kyydissä.

Mayyunin saari sijaitsee Bab el-Mandebin salmella Djiboutin ja Jemenin välissä salmen keskiosassa. Salmi on tärkeä muun muassa öljykuljetuksille. Hallitsemalla sitä huthit voisivat estää Saudi-Arabialta pääsyn Punaisenmeren satamiinsa.

HUTHIEN poliittisen siiven edustaja Hazem al-Assad sanoi perjantai-iltapäivänä, ettei laivaliikenteen suhteen ole syytä huoleen.

- Navigointi ja kansainvälisen kaupan vapaus Punaisellamerellä sekä Bab el-Mandebin salmella ovat turvassa ja järjestyksessä, Al-Assad sanoi.

title: Graduopas-klassikon uusi laitos johdattaa onnistuneeseen graduun ja nostaa esille tekoälyn hyödyt ja riskit
content:
Yksi maisteriopiskelijan suurimmista haasteista on pro gradu -tutkielman laatiminen. Professori ja korkeakoulupedagogiikan dosentti Juha T. Hakalan Graduopas käy havainnollisesti läpi tutkielman tekemisen vaiheet aihevalinnasta aikatauluttamiseen ja lähteiden keräämisestä kirjoittamiseen.

Opiskelijoiden tueksi tehty Graduopas kertoo gradun laadinnasta oleelliset asiat selkeästi, käytännönläheisesti ja realistisesti – huumoria unohtamatta. Kannustava teos auttaa tunnistamaan tyypilliset kompastuskivet ja neuvoo, kuinka ne on mahdollista välttää. Hakala korostaa, että tärkeintä on valmis ja riittävän hyvä opinnäytetyö.

Hakala on ohjannut urallaan yli tuhat pro gradu-tutkielmaa. Ensimmäinen Graduopas julkaistiin jo 1990-luvun lopulla, ja teoksesta on vuosien varrella julkaistu useita päivitettyjä laitoksia. Oppaan uudessa laitoksessa esillä ovat myös tekoälyn hyödyt ja riskit graduntekijän näkökulmasta.

title: Tuula Kaarela-Korhonen rakentaa Äänekosken tulevia kulttuurielämyksiä
content:
Tuula Kaarela-Korhonen on aloittanut elokuussa Äänekosken kaupungin vs. kulttuurituottajana, kun Jukka-Pekka Pohjolainen siirtyi sijaistamaan kulttuuri- ja liikuntajohtajaa.

Kulttuurituottajan työssä Kaarela-Korhonen vastaa kaupungin tapahtumien suunnittelusta ja toteutuksesta sekä niiden viestinnästä ja käytännön järjestelyistä. Työhön kuuluu myös muun muassa tilavarauksia ja viranomaisyhteistyötä lupa-asioissa.

– Nyt Äänekoskella käynnistyvät syyskauden konsertit ja Kulttuuriaitan päiväkotikiertue. Myös ensi kevään ohjelmisto on jo pitkälti suunniteltu. Pääsin heti mukaan toteuttamaan kyläkiertuetta, ja sain tavata mukavia ihmisiä. Äänekoski näyttäytyy minulle lämpimien ihmisten kaupunkina, Kaarela-Korhonen kertoo.

Kaarela-Korhosella on monipuolinen tausta kulttuurin, tapahtumatuotannon, viestinnän ja markkinoinnin parista. Hän on koulutukseltaan kulttuurituottaja (AMK) ja visualisti. Uransa aikana hän on järjestänyt festivaaleja Oulussa, työskennellyt Jyväskylän taidemuseossa ja Teatteri Eurooppa Neljässä sekä viime vuosina viestinnän ja markkinoinnin tehtävissä sosiaali- ja lastensuojelupalveluissa.

Kaarela-Korhonen pääsee alusta asti rakentamaan seuraavan syksyn ohjelmaa.

title: EU Parliament ready to take tougher line on China, says lead MEP
content:
BRUSSELS — A cross-party consensus is growing in the European Parliament on the need for the EU to take a harder line on China, senior MEP Pascal Canfin told POLITICO.

Canfin, the European Parliament’s point person, or rapporteur, on the trade relationship with China, was scathing in his assessment of the threat posed by Beijing’s surging exports.

“The whole purpose of Chinese policy is to be the leader of the new global order based on their own power, their own values and the dictatorship of the Communist Party,” the French liberal said in an interview.

Brussels and Beijing are locked in negotiations over ways to rebalance the bloc’s €1 billion-a-day trade deficit with China. A surge in Chinese exports has put pressure on domestic producers, stoking fears that the continent is deindustrializing amid high-profile factory closures across the automotive and chemical sectors. 

EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič is set to visit Beijing in October as part of the talks. He has said that the bloc stands ready to act if progress is not made by that date.

content:

– Tällä menolla on todellinen vaara, että tulevaisuudessa meillä ei ole suomalaista ruokaa, alan yli 300 000 työpaikkaa eikä huoltovarmuutta ja omavaraisuutta, eduskuntaryhmän puheenjohtaja Antti Kurvinen sanoo keskustan tiedotteessa.

title: Eurooppa tarvitsee suvereenin ja yhteentoimivan digitaalisen koulutusinfrastruktuurin
content:
Eurooppalaisen infrastruktuurin kehittämisessä tulisi ottaa huomioon seuraavat näkökohdat:

  • Vaikka koulutuspaketin painopiste on peruskoulussa, digitaalisen infrastruktuurin tulisi palvella kaikkia koulutusasteita, erityisesti niillä osa-alueilla, joilla haasteet ovat yhteisiä, kuten tiedon keräämisessä ja tuottamisessa.
  • Digitaalisen koulutusinfrastruktuurin rakentaminen ei edellytä uusien keskitettyjen ratkaisujen luomista, vaan pikemminkin olemassa olevien ratkaisujen yhdistämistä, yhteensovittamista ja skaalaamista.
  • Yhteentoimivuus on keskeinen kysymys, jota on tarkasteltava laaja-alaisesti huomioiden kaikki yhteentoimivuuden tasot sekä hyödyntäen olemassa olevia yhteistyörakenteita, kuten korkeakoulutuksen yhteentoimivuuskehystä (Higher Education Interoperability Framework).
  • Jotta koulutussektori voisi hyödyntää tekoälyn tarjoamat lukuisat mahdollisuudet, osana eurooppalaista digitaalista koulutusinfrastruktuuria on kehitettävä turvallisia, toimintavarmoja ja luotettavia tekoälyratkaisuja.

title: Kuka hallitsee dataasi?
content:
Tämä teksti on vieraskynäteksti, joka liittyy 9.9.2026 pidettyyn webinaariimme Datasuvereniteetti – kuka hallitsee dataasi?

Esitän näennäisesti yksinkertaisen kysymyksen: Kuka todella hallitsee dataasi?

Tiedät ehkä, missä datasi sijaitsee ja minkä pilvipalveluntarjoajan palvelussa sitä säilytetään. Mutta tiedätkö, kuka omistaa palveluntarjoajan, minkä lainsäädännön piirissä se toimii ja mitä tapahtuu, jos jokin viranomainen vaatii pääsyä dataasi?

Monille suomalaisille organisaatioille ei ole tarjolla selkeää vastausta.

Olemme rakentaneet suuren osan digitaalisesta infrastruktuuristamme Euroopan ulkopuolisten yritysten varaan. Valitettavasti maailmantilanteen kiristyessä kyse ei ole enää vain teknologiavalinnoista. Kyse on kontrollista ja liiketoimintariskistä.

Amazon, Microsoft ja Google hallitsevat noin 70 prosenttia EU:n pilvimarkkinoista. Lisäksi noin 80 prosenttia eurooppalaisten yritysten yritysohjelmistojen hankinnoista suuntautuu yhdysvaltalaisille toimittajille.

Tähän menestykseen on syynsä. Kyseisillä toimijoilla on ollut käytössään suuret markkinat, pääomaa ja osaamista. Eurooppa puolestaan on pitkälti hyväksynyt syntyneen tilanteen.

title: Kyberkestävyyssäädös tuo valmistajille uuden ilmoitusvelvoitteen ja käyttäjille ajantasaista tietoa tuotteiden kyberturvallisuudesta
content:
Valmistajien uusi ilmoitusvelvoite parantaa käyttäjien mahdollisuuksia saada tietoa tuotteiden vakavista kyberturvallisuusongelmista.

EU:n kyberkestävyyssäädöksen mukainen haavoittuvuuksien ja vakavien tietoturvapoikkeamien ilmoitusvelvoite alkaa 11.9.2026. Valmistajien on ilmoitettava aktiivisesti hyödynnetyistä haavoittuvuuksista ja vakavista tietoturvapoikkeamista Liikenne- ja viestintävirasto Traficomin Kyberturvallisuuskeskukselle ja EU:n kyberturvallisuusvirasto ENISAlle. Valmistajien on lisäksi tiedotettava niistä viipymättä tuotteiden käyttäjille.

Vuonna 2026 EU:n markkinoilla olevista tuotteista on tähän mennessä raportoitu noin 400–500 haavoittuvuutta, jotka olisivat ylittäneet ilmoittamiskynnyksen.

Ilmoittamisvelvoite koskee kaikkia EU:n alueella myytäviä laitteita, myös kolmansista maista maahantuotuja laitteita. Peukalosääntönä voidaan pitää, että jos laite, ohjelmisto tai muu tuote on yhteydessä verkkoon tai toiseen laitteeseen, se kuuluu CRA:n soveltamisalaan.

title: OSI brings the State of the Source to All Things Open 2026
content:
The Open Source Initiative (OSI) is coming to All Things Open with a track designed to connect developers with the big policy conversations shaping our ecosystem. This year’s State of the Source looks at Open Source from several perspectives. Hear about OSI’s priorities for 2027, get a practical introduction to Open Source licensing and compliance, and discuss Open Source sustainability. We’ll also explore the latest public policy developments affecting Open Source, examine the state of Open Source AI, and discuss how OSI can strengthen Open Source education and advocacy.

All Things Open is one of the largest Open Source technology conferences in the United States, bringing together a technical and engaged audience of developers, engineers, community leaders, students, educators, executives, and other Open Source practitioners.

All Things Open 2026 takes place October 19–20 in Raleigh, North Carolina, part of the Research Triangle, one of the country’s leading centers for technology and Open Source innovation.

title: China’s Huawei branded a criminal enterprise as tech firm’s US trial opens
content:
The defense says: ‘It’s about competition, not conspiracy’

A US prosecutor described China’s Huawei as a criminal enterprise that stole from US companies to build its telecommunications empire, as ⁠the trial against the tech company kicked off in Brooklyn federal court on Wednesday.

“Theft, lies, cover-up,” Taylor Stout, a trial attorney from the US Department of Justice, said in the government’s opening statement. “For 20 years, that’s how Huawei, a massive Chinese telecommunications company, victimized American companies ⁠and abused the American financial system, all ⁠in an effort to dominate the telecommunications ​industry around the world.”

title: Uutuuskirja analysoi poliittista viestintää nykypäivän polarisoituneessa Suomessa
content:
Helsingin yliopiston viestinnän professori Juha Herkmanin Poliittinen viestintä polarisaation aikakaudella tarkastelee poliittisen viestinnän tilaa, muotoa ja ajankohtaisia kysymyksiä populismin noususta ja informaatiovaikuttamisesta skandaaleihin ja sosiaaliseen mediaan. Politiikka ja media ovat 2010–2020-luvuilla kohdanneet radikaalimpia muutoksia kuin sitä edeltävän parin vuosikymmenen aikana.

Kansainvälinen poliittinen järjestelmä natisee liitoksissaan, ja kotimaisessa politiikassa edetään kohusta toiseen. Sosiaalinen media on pirstonut poliittisen julkisuuden, ja algoritmit ruokkivat ihmisten ja ihmisryhmien välistä vastakkainasettelua. Geopolitiikasta on tullut keskeinen poliittista viestintää ja päätöksentekoa määrittävä aihe. Minkälaisessa poliittisessa ympäristössä elämme?

”Huomiotaloudessa poliittinen viestintäkulttuuri on kärjistynyt: affektiivista polarisaatiota korostavasta populistisesta tyylistä on tullut poliittisen viestinnän valtavirtaa. Muutokset liittyvät laajempiin yhteiskunnallisiin ongelmiin, kuten globalisaation, uusliberalismin ja geopoliittisten kriisien kansallisvaltioille asettamiin haasteisiin”, Juha Herkman kertoo.
